items.title: ‘They are politically lazy’ – Wike tackles APC govs over Rainbow Coalition pushback
items.description: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has described governors of the All Progressives Congress as “politically lazy” following their opposition to his Rainbow Coalition ahead of the 2027 general elections. The governors, led by their chairman and Imo State Governor, Hope Uzodimma, had said they would not participate in, support or endorse any alliance that could undermine President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid or affect APC candidates at any level. But Wike, in an interview on Arise TV’s Prime Time on Tuesday, dismissed the concerns, arguing that his decision to support Tinubu did not mean he had abandoned his political party or agreed that other parties should not field candidates. “They are politically lazy. When you have your local problems, don’t use Mr President as your excuse,” Wike said. The minister maintained that the disagreements surrounding his political activities did not start with his decision to support Tinubu, recalling that he had faced opposition even when he was serving as governor of Rivers State and later as FCT minister. “This thing did not start today. It started at ministerial position. They were not happy that I was Minister of FCT. Also, they were unhappy when I was governor,” he said. Wike said his knowledge of the political situation was greater than that of those criticising his activities, suggesting that his critics would understand his position better if they had access to the information available to him. “If they know what I know, they would not come out to shout,” he said. The former Rivers State governor also insisted that his support for Tinubu remained unchanged, arguing that supporting the President was separate from the activities of his political party. “I have said I will support the President and I am still supporting him. What has that got to do with my party?” Wike asked. The minister further cited the political activities of governors such as Anambra State Governor Chukwuma Soludo, Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke and Abia State Governor Alex Otti to argue that support for a presidential candidate should not prevent political parties from presenting candidates at other levels. “Take Soludo, Adeleke and Otti. Does it mean that their parties will not present other candidates? This thing they are saying does not have any basis,” he said. Wike also recalled the 2023 presidential election, saying his decision to support Tinubu was based on his belief that it was the South’s turn to produce the President after the Muhammadu Buhari administration. “Recall that in 2023, as far as the President is concerned, it is my belief that it was the time of the South and so it would be unfair that it goes back to the North,” he said. items.title: Saudi says Houthis target Mecca, warn of 'red line'
items.description: The Saudi-led coalition battling Yemen's Houthis accused the rebels on Wednesday of targeting Islam's holy city Mecca, sparking outrage across the Muslim world and deepening the conflict roiling the region. Fresh fighting between the Iran-backed Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni government has dragged in Riyadh, with the Houthis declaring a maritime blockade on the kingdom and targeting its ships in the Red Sea.

items.title: Últimas noches en El Trampolín: la playa de la vergüenza y de las preguntas sin respuesta
items.description: Solo hay una certeza esta noche en la playa del Trampolín: nadie quiere estar aquí y nadie quiere que estén aquí. Todo lo demás en este trozo de costa es una especulación, un bullir de preguntas que opaca el sonido del mar en esta madrugada un mes y medio después. No está claro cuántos son los migrantes que la habitan –las últimas estimaciones lo sitúan en 4.000– ni si esta es la crónica de la última noche que dormirán en la orilla. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Interior prepara la instalación de dos centros de identificación permanentes para migrantes en Ceuta y Melilla con 800 plazas cada uno
items.description: Dos meses y medio después de la entrada masiva en Ceuta , el Gobierno trabaja en dos flancos complementarios: acelerar la instalación de los emplazamientos para realojar a los migrantes con el propósito de sacarlos de la calle y, a la vez, identificarlos dentro de esos recursos para agilizar los trámites de expulsión. Porque los expedientes de retorno se inician una vez se haya completado la filiación individual de cada persona. El presidente Sánchez anunció el lunes por la noche, en una entrevista en La Sexta, que el propósito es habilitar 10.000 plazas en suelo ceutí. Ese número comprende tanto las camas temporales que están siendo habilitadas estos días —y cuya instalación continúa—, como otro establecimiento que prepara Interior con 800 camas para realizar los procesos de identificación y que se instalará de forma permanente. En paralelo, en Melilla se establecerá otro centro de triaje con el mismo aforo y ambos podrán facilitarse con el impulso de la financiación europea. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Restaurantes, contratos ficticios y subidas de sueldo: el exolímpico Carles Sala, señalado por un agujero de 150.000 euros en una entidad deportiva
items.description: El Consell Esportiu del Barcelonès Nord (Cebnord), un órgano privado que se nutre de fondos públicos y que promueve el deporte escolar en Badalona, Santa Coloma y Sant Adrià, ha abierto expediente disciplinario y despedido al que fue hasta hace poco su máximo responsable operativo: el exatleta olímpico Carles Sala . Tras elaborar una auditoría por los números rojos de los últimos años, el Consell acusa a Sala de actuaciones “negligentes”, “fraudulentas” y “absolutamente inaceptables” que han ocasionado un perjuicio de 150.000 euros, según la documentación a la que ha accedido EL PAÍS, lo que ha dejado a la entidad en una situación económica “crítica”. Seguir leyendo

Así definía The New York Times al streamer y comentarista político Hasan Piker (Nueva Jersey, 35 años) en una entrevista que subrayaba que sus exigentes rutinas de ejercicio (cuya figura es fruto de un antes y después de libro) se asemejan a las de los fitness influencers, cuya ideología tiende a virar hacia hacia lo conservador . items.title: Eduard Sola, guionista: “A las madres les hemos robado la sexualidad y tenemos que devolvérsela”
items.description: Hace dos años, Eduard Sola (Santa Eulàlia de Ronçana, Barcelona, 37 años) fue el hombre que lo escribió todo en el cine y la tele españoles. Firmar los guiones de Casa en llamas , La virgen roja y Querer lo sacó de un relativo anonimato y lo convirtió en uno de los profesionales más solicitados del cine español. Luego llegó otra clase de fama: su discurso en los Premios Gaudí, donde se definió como “orgullosamente charnego” y reivindicó la capacidad de integración de la sociedad catalana. La polémica posterior lo desbordó. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Aquí no puede votar cualquiera
items.description: Como esos supertacañones que defendían que una cosa era la libertad y otra, el libertinaje, el Supremo —con la salvedad bravísima y triste de la magistrada Alicia Millán, única discrepante— ha dicho que una cosa es votar y otra muy distinta, el voteo al buen tuntún . ¿Qué es eso de que cualquier ciudadano español pueda meter una papeleta en una urna? El derecho al sufragio, señores míos, es algo muy serio. No sabemos qué piensan todos esos nietos de aquella ralea de exiliados. Vaya usted a saber a qué propaganda están sometidos. No a la nuestra, desde luego. Esa gente no sigue las tertulias de la radio. A lo peor, tienen una visión de España filtrada por las batallitas de sus abuelos, enemigos sin matices del franquismo, al que no le verían nada bueno. Viven aturdidos por Bad Bunny y Shakira, no les suena ni un estribillo de Manolo Escobar. Seguir leyendo

items.title: “No tiene conexión”
items.description: Intento entrar a primera hora del lunes 7 de septiembre en mi cuenta de Caixabank a través del móvil y me aparece un aviso que dice: “No tiene conexión”. Como la aplicación me está hablando a mí, y por edad ya merezco que me traten de usted, pienso lógicamente que quien no tiene conexión soy yo, que se ha estropeado mi red doméstica, o la del teléfono, o la del barrio, qué sé yo. Pero pruebo con otro banco, y con elpais.com, y envío mensajes, y reviso el correo… Todo funciona. O sea, que sí tengo conexión. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Las nuevas leyes de dependencia y discapacidad afrontan su último paso en el Congreso: más cuidados en casa, menos burocracia
items.description: La mayor reforma en los 20 años de historia de la ley de dependencia está a solo un paso de ver la luz. Prevé nuevos servicios, como el de cuidados y apoyos en viviendas para personas con grandes necesidades de apoyo; mejoras en otros ya existentes, como la ayuda a domicilio —que podrá salir de las casas para acompañar a los usuarios a gestiones como hacer la compra—, y también reducir la burocracia, al crear una pasarela que permita obtener directamente un certificado de un 33% o un 65% de discapacidad, si ya se tiene alguno de los grados de dependencia reconocido. Este miércoles, el Congreso votará si acepta o no las enmiendas introducidas la semana pasada en el Senado, donde el PP tiene mayoría. En el mismo proyecto también se modifica la ley de discapacidad, en la que se reconoce la accesibilidad universal como derecho, por lo que podrá reivindicarse ante cualquier instancia. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Interior evita el choque y asume que Balas siga al frente de las investigaciones que afectan al PSOE
items.description: Despejada la última duda sobre el futuro papel del recién ascendido coronel Antonio Balas en la Unidad Central Operativa (UCO) de la Guardia Civil. La dirección general del instituto armado ha publicado este martes en su boletín oficial una relación de 71 vacantes de teniente coronel para ser ocupadas por el procedimiento de libre designación en la que no figura la de jefe del Departamento de Investigación Económica y Anticorrupción de esta unidad, la plaza que ocupaba el ahora coronel Balas hasta su ascenso. La decisión del Ministerio del Interior supone que el oficial ―que al ascender debía cambiar de destino a un puesto de su nuevo rango y, por tanto, dejar las pesquisas― no solo se encargue de la investigación para la que el juez de la Audiencia Nacional Ismael Moreno pidió expresamente que siguiera al frente, el caso Koldo , sino también del resto de causas, aunque los magistrados que las dirigen no hubieran solicitado expresamente su continuidad. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Así se paró ‘in extremis’ el desahucio de Hubrimar y su hijo de 9 años
items.description: Hubrimar Medina no sabía si esa noche podría dormir en su cama. Tiene 29 años, nació en Venezuela y llegó a Madrid hace una década. Lleva seis años viviendo bajo el mismo techo, un piso en el distrito madrileño de Tetuán , en la calle de Jaén, 25. Ha pagado su alquiler todos los meses, pero no a quien debía. Un anterior inquilino la estafó y le hizo creer que era el verdadero propietario, cuando en realidad la vivienda pertenece al fondo de inversión Blackstone, que ahora la quiere desahuciar. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La Diócesis de Getafe decreta la supresión de una asociación religiosa denunciada por presuntos exorcismos y agresiones sexuales
items.description: La Diócesis de Getafe ha puesto fin al proyecto de los Hermanos del Amor Misericordioso, la rama masculina de la comunidad investigada por graves denuncias de abusos sexuales, de poder y de conciencia, aislamiento y penitencias físicas. La decisión obliga a los sacerdotes, diáconos y seminaristas que desde 2008 vivían y se formaban juntos, con la aspiración de constituirse en congregación religiosa, a continuar sus caminos por separado. El cierre se produce mes y medio después de que la Archidiócesis de Madrid suprimiera la rama femenina al considerar inviable su continuidad. El obispo de Getafe atribuye la medida a “un tiempo prolongado de reflexión y acompañamiento”, pero no menciona las denuncias presentadas por antiguos integrantes ni explica qué ha precipitado ahora la decisión. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Los planes para restringir el uso de las redes a los menores, país por país
items.description: El debate sobre la prohibición del acceso de los menores de 15 años a las redes sociales está presente en Europa desde noviembre de 2025, cuando Dinamarca comenzó a estudiar, siguiendo la estela de Australia, la posibilidad de restringirlo por completo. Desde entonces, varios países europeos han impulsado distintas iniciativas para limitar el acceso de los menores a estas plataformas. Ahora, la Comisión Europea prepara una propuesta común para que los menores de 15 años no puedan acceder a las redes sociales sin autorización paterna y, a partir de esa edad, puedan hacerlo por sí mismos solo en un entorno seguro. items.title: Drones superrápidos de motor a reacción, el arma rusa ante la que Ucrania no está preparada
items.description: El signo de una guerra guarda en ocasiones más relación con la iniciativa que con el combate. Ucrania es buen ejemplo. La superioridad de Rusia, sobre el papel, debiera haber finiquitado el conflicto en poco tiempo, pero la creatividad y el factor sorpresa han permitido a Kiev mantener el pulso. Aunque no siempre. Cunde últimamente la sensación de que los interceptores ucranios no son capaces de hacer frente a los potentes drones de motor a reacción rusos. Según datos de la Fuerza Aérea ucrania, cuatro de cada diez vehículos de ataque de este tipo, con velocidades de hasta 600 kilómetros por hora y una carga explosiva de 90 kilogramos, vuelan hasta su objetivo con éxito. El agujero defensivo es grande. Una de estas aeronaves fue la que alcanzó un centro comercial de Krivói Rog el pasado 21 de agosto , después de que un primer aparato golpease unos minutos antes los almacenes. 16 personas perdieron la vida. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El velo retrocede en Irán, pero el sistema resiste: “Nosotras ya hemos demostrado que podemos luchar”
items.description: Golnar entra con una camisa rosa de manga corta, un pantalón azul ancho, su pelo ondulado al aire y se sienta en una de las mesas codiciadas de uno de los cafés más populares en el área central de Teherán , donde muchas veces hay que esperar hasta encontrar sitio. Por seguridad, ha advertido de que no dará su nombre verdadero y quiere que se le identifique como Golnar. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Cómo recuperar la rutina de sueño de los niños en septiembre y por qué acostarles antes no siempre funciona
items.description: Septiembre pone a prueba uno de los cambios más difíciles del comienzo de curso : volver a madrugar cuando el cuerpo todavía no se ha acostumbrado al nuevo horario. Después de semanas de horarios flexibles, noches largas y mañanas sin despertador, recuperar el descanso no se consigue acostando a los niños de golpe a una hora más temprana, sino ayudando a su organismo a adaptarse de forma gradual. ¿Por qué volver a madrugar resulta, año tras año, tan difícil? Seguir leyendo

items.title: Maquinaria de crueldad
items.description: Cuando Donald Trump regresó al poder en 2025 y la Casa Blanca anunció la “mayor operación de deportaciones de la historia de Estados Unidos”, se puso en marcha una maquinaria de crueldad que en menos de dos años ha destruido familias y proyectos de vida en vecindarios por todo el país con detenciones masivas y sin criterio alguno. La parte más visible de esta xenofobia oficial han sido las exhibiciones de violencia por parte de la policía migratoria, ICE, un pequeño cuerpo de policía judicial transformado por el presidente estadounidense en una fuerza dedicada al acoso y la persecución arbitraria y brutal de los inmigrantes. Pero la parte más oculta sucede después de esas detenciones. La obsesión por infundir terror ha llevado a la Administración de EE UU a operar al margen de la ley para evitar las garantías constitucionales que asisten a cualquier persona, también a las indocumentadas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: ‘Ley de nietos’: hambre, terror y represión en la posguerra española
items.description: El dibujante madrileño Carlos Giménez ha retratado el hambre y el terror de la posguerra española a través de su serie de cómics autobiográficos Paracuellos (Reservoir Books), una de las obras más significativas sobre el franquismo, que empezó a publicar en 1976, poco después de la muerte del dictador, y que mantiene todavía viva, según siguen emergiendo sus recuerdos. Los niños internados en un Auxilio Social de Madrid sufrían palizas constantes por parte de los sádicos instructores de la Falange, pero, por encima de todo, tenían hambre: todos los días, a todas horas… A sus 85 años, Giménez cuenta que “ya se le ha acabado el rencor” al evocar aquellos años de violencia y fascismo, pero que “el hambre nunca se termina de quitar del todo”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Madrid ataca al cirujano denunciante del Ramón y Cajal y reduce el escándalo a una rencilla entre médicos
items.description: El Ejecutivo de Isabel Díaz Ayuso ha reducido el último escándalo en su sanidad a disputas entre médicos. Su consejera de Sanidad, Fátima Matute, fue la encargada de anunciar al término de la jornada del martes que están investigando si dos responsables en el Hospital Ramón y Cajal rebajaron la prioridad de las cirugías a pacientes en lista de espera a espaldas de los médicos que habían valorado a esos enfermos, como había revelado EL PAÍS. Pero la propia Matute cuestionó la credibilidad del denunciante, el cirujano Luis Alberto Martos, y adelantó el desenlace: todo es correcto, según dijo. La presidenta, Isabel Díaz Ayuso, no se pronunció, pero una fuente de su entorno atribuyó lo sucedido a un choque entre facultativos: “Cosas entre ellos”, respondió por mensaje. Seguir leyendo

items.title: ‘Fondue’, solomillo a la pimienta y panteras rosas: cómo la Transición nos cambió a través del plato
items.description: Parte de la revolución española de los setenta y ochenta ocurrió alrededor de las cocinas de formica y las de algunos restaurantes. Entre el borboteo de la nueva olla exprés y el olor a sofrito de toda la vida , España pasó en pocas décadas de la escasez a la abundancia, del bocata de jamón o el pan con vino y azúcar a la llegada masiva de la bollería industrial ; todo aliñado con novedades como el túrmix, los Tupperware o el microondas. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Claire-Louise Bennet: “En la experiencia amorosa debería estar la diferencia, el azar y el riesgo, algo casi imposible en un mundo de ‘apps’ de ligar”
items.description: Le interesa, ha dicho, de qué forma existimos en la mente de los demás. Qué somos, también, cuando solo somos una idea. Quizá por eso, su narrativa pasa, siempre, por la mente de alguien. Un alguien que, obsesivamente, trata de encontrar una salida. O de situarse en el mundo. ¿Es el amor algún tipo de brújula? ¿Orienta, cada vez de forma distinta, al yo? Claire-Louise Bennett (Wiltshire, Reino Unido) cree que debería hacerlo, pero también cree que cada vez le dejamos que lo haga menos. Las aplicaciones no son de ninguna ayuda, dice. En su última novela, la intensa, laberíntica y poderosamente interior, Besos, chao (Malas Tierras), se pregunta de qué manera el amor te coloca ante un espejo y te muestra aquello que jamás admitirías que también eres. Y a algo así solo puede llegarse, como diría Anaïs Nin , a partir del misterio de aquello que te atrae del otro cuando nada está pactado de antemano. En su casa de Galway, Irlanda, Bennett —autora también de La caja 19 (Malas Tierras) y Estanque (Eterna Cadencia)— descuelga la videollamada. Está sentada ante una mesa enorme. Está cubierta de cuadernos, y esferas de cristal. Tiene cerca, dice, incluso un pingüino de vidrio. Y la taza de la que sorbe de vez en cuando contiene aún parte del té Yogi Choco que se hizo hace un rato. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La vivienda perfecta y barata: la utopía que la arquitectura lleva un siglo prometiendo
items.description: En 1927, el arquitecto e inventor estadounidense Richard Buckminster Fuller gritó a los cuatro vientos una idea que sonaba a broma: la posibilidad de tener una casa al mismo precio que un coche. Así nació la Dymaxion House: un armazón hexagonal de aluminio, ligero como una tienda de campaña, pensado para fabricarse en una cadena de montaje igual que un Ford. Buckminster Fuller (1895-1983) estaba convencido de que la vivienda tradicional era ineficiente y cara, y de que la misma industria que había puesto el automóvil al alcance de la clase media podía hacer lo propio con el techo bajo el que dormían; sin embargo, a pesar de los miles de pedidos que llegó a recibir, solo se construyeron dos prototipos. items.title: ¿Qué es Anthropic y por qué se ha convertido en un gigante de la IA?
Politics and protests
items.description: IT is the same tired play. As soon as the opposition announces a protest, the government reflexively cracks down. Citizens are roughed up and arrested, and the security officials who round them up later collect medals for their services. There are no consequences for this abuse of state power. Indeed, it increasingly appears that the lead-up to a protest, and not the protest itself, is where the real political battle is fought. And all this is playing out at the moment on television screens and social media, as the PTI prepares for its Sept 27 march on Islamabad to demand its jailed founder’s release. The machinery of the state has kicked into action all over the country, armed with the usual pretexts of ‘prevention of violence’ and ‘protection of public infrastructure and property’. The actions taken to thwart the march appear to be many. At least 155, perhaps more, preventive detention orders have been issued under the MPO; lists have been drawn up of PTI leaders and workers for further ‘preventive arrests’; police personnel’s leaves have been cancelled; containers and roadblocks are being prepared ; restrictions have been placed on rallies and public gatherings; and Section 144 has been implemented in Punjab , with plans of a broader rollout soon. Authorities undoubtedly have a responsibility to maintain order, and reasonable measures to discharge that responsibility are legitimate. But half a dozen overlapping instruments, deployed against a political party’s leadership and rank and file, cannot be considered reasonable by any stretch. Sadly, such actions only give the impression that even calls for protest are considered a thought crime in our society. The heavy-handedness with which the government has been curtailing the opposition’s ability to exercise its lawful political rights should not be overlooked. Every democracy allows its citizens to express their will in different ways, including through peaceful public protests. That the government can and will prosecute political leaders and workers who actually break the law is not in dispute; the state has every right to respond firmly when violent protest tactics are employed deliberately. However, the point is that deterrents already exist and do not require the pre-emptive detention of people who have broken no law. Past protests may have turned violent, but that history cannot be used as a justification to arbitrarily suspend constitutional rights for those who have caused no offence. It is time to stop treating dissent as a security threat and allow the public a peaceful outlet to air its grievances. The consequences of not ceding that space gracefully will only grow more severe with time. A government confident in its own legitimacy does not need to criminalise the mere anticipation of a protest. Ours, evidently, is not that confident. Published in Dawn, September 16th, 2026

items.title: Novartis backs Ghana Medical Trust Fund, eyes partnership to expand specialist care
items.description: Global healthcare company Novartis has expressed support for the Ghana Medical Trust Fund (GMTF), describing the initiative as a critical intervention to improve access to specialised healthcare. The President of Global Health and Swiss Country Director of Novartis, Dr Lutz Hegeman, made the remarks while leading a delegation from the company to engage with the management of the Trust Fund. Dr Hegeman said Novartis is prepared to collaborate with the GMTF to help more Ghanaians living with chronic diseases access financial support for specialised treatment. He also expressed interest in partnerships in research and development, as well as the provision of medical equipment and training for healthcare professionals. According to him, the objectives of the GMTF align closely with Novartis’ work in specialised healthcare. The engagement also provided an opportunity for the Administrator of the GMTF, Adjoa Obuobia Darko-Opoku, to outline the Fund’s achievements since its establishment a year ago. Among the milestones, she highlighted the commissioning of an ultra-modern Cardiac Catheterisation Laboratory at the National Cardiothoracic Centre of the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital. She also cited the donation of medical equipment and consumables to the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital, as well as the ongoing construction of cardiology centres at the Komfo Anokye and Tamale Teaching Hospitals. Ms Darko-Opoku said the Trust Fund had also begun providing financial support directly to accredited treatment centres to help patients meet the cost of high-cost chronic care. The support covers conditions and treatments, including dialysis, cancer treatment, renal care, and cardiovascular diseases, that fall outside the National Health Insurance Scheme. “We have also spearheaded ongoing specialist medical training and efforts to bridge critical equipment deficits, including MRI and CT scanners, in regional facilities,” she said. The discussions are expected to strengthen collaboration between Novartis and the GMTF in specialised healthcare, research and development, medical equipment and professional training.

items.title: Employee claims facing police ire for saying Mir Raza didn’t use drugs
items.description: KARACHI: An employee of businessman Mir Raza Ali told a judicial commission on Tuesday that he faced investigators’ anger after saying the deceased did not use drugs. The Judicial Commission in the Mir Raza murder case continued its proceedings on Tuesday and recorded statements of a police officer, an employee of the deceased and his two investors. The one-member commission headed by Justice Omar Sial of the Sindh High Court also expressed displeasure over a focal person of the provincial government and police for still not providing the complete record of the case to the commission despite repeated directives. In his testimony, the manager of the victim’s eatery Wafflix, Shahryar, said that he was working at the Bahadurabad branch for the last two years and reporting to the victim who treated him like a younger brother. Wafflix manager tells judicial commission parts of his police statements were ‘incorrectly’ attributed to him Responding to a question of the commission about losses to the business of the deceased, he deposed that the sales had been declining for the past few months and the salaries of the staff were also delayed during the last couple of months, but he did not find the victim worried during his last interactions with him. He said that the daily sales were around Rs100,000, but they had fallen to Rs75,000 to Rs70,000 during the last two months. He also said that police had recorded his statements twice and his phone was also seized by the second investigation team on Aug 17, adding that his first statement was written on a paper on Aug 2 and the second testimony was recorded through video. The witness further submitted that the police had asked questions about the business and the family issues of the victim. He said the first team had misbehaved with him while SP Qais, who is said to be a part of the second team, had also come down hard on him when he had informed the team that the victim was not using any drugs. The commission pointed out that he had provided complete details and figures about the business of the deceased to the police, but did not provide the same to the commission, which contradicted his testimonies recorded by the police. He submitted that the police did not read out such statements to him and some additions were incorrectly attributed to him. The manager also deposed that the victim along with his business partner Ahmed Bhardey had gone to Hyderabad to attend a party arranged by a catering firm on July 25 and came back on the following day while the victim had taken Rs29,000 from him around midnight of July 27 and left the branch. He further testified that he had closed the branch on the same night around 3:30am and at around 4:10am Bhardey had asked him regarding Raza’s whereabouts. He maintained that on July 28, another employee had informed him that a pistol of a security guard of the eatery, kept at the shop, was missing and they came to know through the footage that Raza came to the branch last night after it was closed and took the weapon. However, he said that as per his knowledge, the victim had never used any weapon and he had no dispute with any vendor, creditor or investor. At the outset of the hearing, Inspector Muhammad Ali turned up and deposed that he was posted at the investigation section of District South and co-opted by the current police team investigating the case as it was his responsibility to assist the team. He also said that he was told to file a letter when he had gone to collect the post-mortem report from the hospital and despite submitting the letter, he did not get the report since the officer concerned was said to be out of the city. Replying to a query of the commission, the police officer further testified that the investigating officer had gone to Hyderabad when he had sought the autopsy report in order to submit it to the investigation team. Muhammad Hassan Khan Tanoli, who recorded his statement via video link from Australia, said that he and Raza had been friends since school and initially, he had provided Rs500,000 to the victim and he had returned the same within the given period along with some profit. Thereafter, he also deposed that he had given him Rs7.5 million as he was willing to import containers of chocolates as well as expanding business. The victim had handed over some cheques to him and advised him not to deposit them since he would arrange the money. The witness further testified that he had contacted Ahmed Bhardey through social media after Raza had gone missing and later also spoke to the father of the victim. The commission asked him that Mr Bhardey in his statement said that he (Hassan) had demanded the return of the money in question from him. He replied that he had only informed the business partner of the victim that he had provided money or a loan to Raza. He had admitted that the victim had borrowed such money for Wafflix while Bhardey had claimed that he was not aware of such an investment. Asad Ali Butt deposed that he had first met the victim in 2016-17 and he had established an outlet in Bahadurabad in 2022 and he had also encouraged people to invest in it. He also said that he had also made an investment of Rs2.5m with Wafflix and all the transactions were made through the account of his mother. During the hearing, the counsel for Raza’s family Jibran Nasir informed the commission that the victim’s father, Mir Hussain Ali, had received a phone call last night and the caller had identified himself as a security official of an institution. The counsel said that the caller had asked Mir Hussain whether he suspected Ahmed Bhardey and Abdullah Bhardey or Asif and his brother Abid as the accused persons. However, he told the caller that the matter was being investigated by the police and therefore, the caller expressed displeasure and disconnected the call, he added. The lawyer said that he has submitted the screenshots and call recording to the registrar of the commission. Published in Dawn, September 16th, 2026

items.title: CDH : l'ONU alerte sur la menace systémique des "polluants éternels"
items.description: Devant la 63e session du Conseil des droits de l'homme des Nations Unies à Genève, deux experts indépendants de l'ONU ont tiré la sonnette d'alarme concernant la prolifération des substances per- et polyfluoroalkylées (PFAS). Ces composants chimiques de synthèse, surnommés « polluants éternels » en raison de leur extrême persistance environnementale, font l'objet d'un plaidoyer pour une interdiction rapide de leurs usages non essentiels à l'échelle mondiale. Présentant le rapport élaboré par son prédécesseur Marcos Orellana, la nouvelle Rapporteuse spéciale sur les substances toxiques et les droits de l'homme, Bethanie Carney Almroth, a souligné la quasi-impossibilité d'éliminer ces composés une fois dispersés dans la nature. Capables de parcourir de longues distances via l'air et l'eau, les PFAS subsistent dans les écosystèmes pendant plusieurs siècles sans qu'aucune technologie actuelle ne permette un assainissement à grande échelle. Urgence sanitaire et contamination cumulative des ressources en eau La contamination ne touche pas uniquement les zones industrielles périphériques. Présents dans la chaîne alimentaire, les produits de consommation courante et les réseaux d'eau potable, ces composés constituent une menace directe pour la santé publique. L'exposition aux PFAS engendre des conséquences sanitaires graves et irréversibles : – Transmission néonatale : capacité avérée des PFAS à traverser la barrière placentaire, avec une présence détectée dans le sang du cordon ombilical et le lait maternel. – Perturbations endocriniennes : atteintes directes aux systèmes hormonaux, altération des fonctions hépatiques et affaiblissement de la réponse immunitaire. – Toxicité cumulative : effet cocktail aggravé par l'association des PFAS aux métaux lourds et aux pesticides dans les sources d'eau potable, affectant particulièrement le développement infantile. Lors de son allocution finale, le Rapporteur spécial sur le droit à l'eau potable et à l'assainissement, Pedro Arrojo-Agudo, a qualifié cette crise de « pollution mortelle », appelant à une cartographie rigoureuse des zones d'eau contaminées au niveau international. Justice environnementale et application du principe pollueur-payeur Les intervenants ont inscrit la gestion des PFAS au cœur des enjeux de justice environnementale. Majoritairement produites au sein des nations industrialisées, ces molécules se propagent à l'échelle globale par le commerce et les transferts transfrontaliers de déchets, impactant de manière disproportionnée les populations vulnérables et les pays du Sud. Face à ce constat, les experts de l'ONU invitent les gouvernements à abandonner l'attentisme réglementaire au profit d'une approche préventive stricte. Le rapport préconise l'interdiction immédiate de l'usage des PFAS dès lors qu'ils ne répondent pas à des besoins sociétaux vitaux, tout en exigeant l'application rigoureuse du principe pollueur-payeur aux secteurs de l'extraction minière, de l'industrie chimique et de l'agriculture intensive. The post CDH : l'ONU alerte sur la menace systémique des "polluants éternels" appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Opposition, treasury in Sindh Assembly unite to demand Centre stop daily petroleum price hikes
items.description: • PTI resolution states daily fluctuations in global oil prices should not be passed on to consumers as Pakistan does not import petrol every day • Sharjeel urges MQM-P to press federal govt for withdrawal of Rs100-plus petroleum levy KARACHI: The Sindh Assembly, otherwise divided along bitter party lines, on Tuesday unanimously demanded through a resolution that the federal government immediately stop the practice of increasing petroleum prices on a daily basis, saying that no new shipment or import of petrol arrives in the country every day to justify it. The resolution, tabled by Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf (PTI) lawmaker Muhammad Owais, said that daily fluctuations in international oil prices should not be passed on to consumers on a daily basis, as Pakistan did not import petrol daily. The resolution said that the continuous increase in petrol prices was fuelling inflation and the common man was facing severe hardship. It said, “This House demands that the federal government immediately stop the daily increase in petroleum product prices,” adding that no new shipment or import of petrol arrived in Pakistan on a daily basis to justify passing on daily fluctuations in international prices. The resolution demanded that stability be brought to petroleum prices to provide relief to the public and that the practice of daily price hikes be ended forthwith. This was the second adopted resolution related to petroleum products in the current session of the assembly. Speaking on his resolution, the PTI member also demanded the withdrawal of the Rs100-plus petroleum levy through a unanimously adopted resolution. Supporting the resolution, Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon said that people were distressed due to rising petroleum prices and the federal government was charging over Rs100 per litre as a levy, which should be withdrawn. He asked the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P), an ally of the federal government, to take up the issue with the Centre to provide relief to the people. Recalling that the MQM had once quit the PPP-led federal government in 2008 over a one-rupee increase in petrol price, he said the party was now silently enjoying power. “Those who are sitting in the federal cabinet should speak on this issue,” he said. The senior minister said that the PPP fully supported the resolution and demanded that the federal government abolish the levy and “come to its senses” on petroleum pricing. He said that MQM-P’s federal representatives should explain why they were not raising their voice against petroleum inflation. ‘PM’s Rs100 subsidy on petrol not sufficient’ Later, speaking to reporters at the Media Corner on the premises of the assembly, provincial government spokesperson Sadia Javed said the federal government’s plan to give a Rs100 subsidy on petrol for certain categories was not sufficient and would not benefit the poor. She said that the prime minister should improve the FBR’s performance and reduce the Rs125 per litre tax on petrol, as only a direct cut in prices would provide genuine relief. She argued that petrol was not used only by the elite but also by goods transport, and unless transport costs came down, food prices would not fall. Ms Javed also lashed out at Federal Minister Mustafa Kamal, terming him “extremely ill-mannered” for cursing politics, and said that if he hated politics so much he should quit politics and resign from his ministry. She questioned why he had not resigned over the deaths of children at PIMS Hospital. Adjournment motion During proceedings, an adjournment motion by MQM-P MPA Amir Siddiqui regarding the sale of narcotics under flyovers and bridges was rejected by a member of the Panel of Chairmen, Dr Sikandar Shoro, after opposition from the government. Mr Siddiqui said that drugs were being sold openly under flyovers and bridges. He said that the menace was also affecting educational institutions, including schools and colleges. PPP MPA Heer Soho opposed the motion, saying an adjournment motion had to relate to a recent occurrence and the motion did not meet the criteria. Education Minister said the assembly’s standing committee on home had already taken up the issue and action was being taken in this regard. “Let the result come,” he said. Excise Minister Mukesh Chawala also opposed the adjournment motion, saying that the house had already debated the issue at length and the government was working to contain the menace. The chair said that the motion was not maintainable and ruled it out of order. Question Hour Earlier, during the Question Hour, Women Development Minister Shaheena Sher Ali said that complaint centres were functioning at the divisional level across the province and offices were also set up in every district. “Five to 15 complaints were received daily, and prompt action was taken on them,” she added. The minister said that women were being imparted training through a revolving fund and two day-care centres were functioning in Karachi with a prescribed age limit for admission. “Awareness is being created about helpline 1094,” she added. Replying to a question, she said there was no day-care centre inside the Sindh Assembly, but one was functioning near the Karachi Press Club. Dr Sikandar Shoro, who was presiding over the sitting as a member of the Panel of Chairmen, observed that the assembly should also have a day-care centre. The minister said that the department would establish one if space was provided. Several other items on the assembly business agenda, including three other resolutions and as many private motions of the opposition members, did not come up as the house was adjourned immediately after the unanimous passage of the resolution against the petroleum levy. The house was later adjourned till Friday. Published in Dawn, September 16th, 2026

items.title: Oil falls as US crude inventories rise despite Saudi supply concerns
items.description: Oil prices fell on Wednesday after an unexpected build in U.S. crude inventories, while investors assessed supply risks after Saudi Arabia suspended ​oil loadings at its Yanbu port following an attack on its East-West pipeline ‌to the Red Sea. Brent crude futures fell 93 cents, or 0.86%, to $107.82 a barrel at 0028 GMT, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures were down 97 cents, or 0.92%, at $104.86 a barrel. Both benchmarks settled more ​than $3 higher and at their highest levels since May 19 on Tuesday, as ​the Yanbu loading suspension stoked supply concerns and Saudi Arabia cut oil shipments ⁠to Europe U.S. crude oil, gasoline and distillate inventories all rose last week, market sources said on ​Tuesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute. Crude inventories rose by 7.1 million barrels in ​the week ended September 11, the sources said, citing API data. That compared with analysts’ expectations for a draw of about 1.6 million barrels, according to a Reuters poll. API’s data showed unexpected builds in gasoline and diesel inventories, which have weighed on prices, but regional stock increases do not change the underlying tightness in the global crude market, Haitong Futures said in a note. Sources said on Tuesday that oil loadings ‌at ⁠Saudi Arabia’s Yanbu port had been suspended after the world’s biggest crude exporter shut its East-West pipeline following an attack by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis on Friday. Saudi Arabia has used the pipeline to reroute around 4 million barrels per day, or about 4% of global supply, to the Red ​Sea port. The U.S. energy ​secretary said crude ⁠should resume flowing through Saudi Arabia’s vital East-West pipeline within days. However, sources who spoke to Reuters gave varying estimates of how long the pipeline could ​remain offline. One said repairs could take five to six weeks, ​while another said ⁠the pipeline could resume partial pumping sooner as repairs continue. In Libya, unrelated to the Iran conflict, the National Oil Corporation (NOC) said operations at three oil fields were suspended after protesting members of the Petroleum Facilities Guard shut off a valve on the Hamada-Zawiya crude export pipeline. However, Libya’s oil production has not been significantly affected by the shutdowns and remains at about 1.4 million ​barrels per day, NOC Chairman Massoud Suleman told Reuters.

items.title: Magazine that was 132 years overdue returned to US library
items.description: A 19th century magazine borrowed from a library in New Hampshire 132 years ago has finally been returned. Concord Public Library said the overdue September 1894 issue of The Century Illustrated Monthly Magazine was returned last week after the library announced a freeze on fines. The magazine was 48,220 days overdue and would have incurred a $12,055 (£8,950) fine. The patron who returned the magazine, John, said it had been “hanging around” his house for decades, but he had no idea how it had ended up there. He decided to return the magazine after reading about the library’s fine freeze in the local newspaper. “We’ve witnessed many happy faces since announcing our fine freeze,” Concord Public Library wrote on Facebook. “Of course, we expected long overdue books to be returned, but certainly not something from the late 19th century!” Concord Public Library declared a year-long amnesty on overdue fines from 1 September 2026, with plans to evaluate the effects of a “fine-free library”. “Understandably, it won’t be placed back in circulation, but perhaps it deserves a spot in the Concord Room,” the post on social media said, referring to a section of the library dedicated to local history. “Thankfully, he won’t have to pay the $12,055 fine for being 48,220 days overdue.”

items.title: Igbo identity crisis: The DNA option (2), by Ochereome Nnanna
items.description: Since the end of the Biafra War in January 1970, ethnic disunity has wreaked great havoc in the former Eastern Region. In the former Northern Region, the Minorities (especially Christians and non-Muslims) want to be fully accepted by the so-called “Hausa/Fulani” Muslim Majority, who wield overwhelming power. But they (the Minorities) are rebuffed, discriminated against and subjugated. The same applies to the Minorities in the old Western Region. The Yoruba tend to keep the Edoid and Western Igbo groups at arm’s length. Only the Itsekiri are spared this because of real or contrived “ancestral links”. In the East, the situation is the other way round. The Minorities distance themselves from their Igbo Majority neighbours. The situation is so queer that even those who are obviously Igbo (in terms of names, language and culture) reject the tag of Igbo. They rather hold strongly to their dialectal identity, which they call “ethnic nationality”. When an Igbo-speaking Ikwerre or Ukwuani person denies being Igbo, it is as laughable as me, an Abiriba man, claiming, “I am Abiriba; I am not Igbo.” In our first instalment of this article, I gave examples of how these false claims have always failed to fool other non-Igbo Nigerians when political decisions are being made. Peter Odili, an Igbo identity denier, was swept aside by President Olusegun Obasanjo in favour of Goodluck Jonathan, despite being obviously more endowed with leadership qualities than Jonathan. The Eastern people, irrespective of subtle differences, have always stood out from the rest of the country in many ways. They share the same republican, democratic culture. Some groups are monarchical; others were historically led by a committee of elders under a paramount figure, an Obi or Eze. There were no absolute kings anywhere in the East. There was absolutely no imperial or expansionist culture. No community sought to conquer and annex the other. Quarrels were settled according to laid-down traditions. People interacted, intermarried and traded freely. Up till today, the cultural dressing of all Eastern groups, from Igbo to Ibibio/Efik to Ijo to Ogoni, remains a shared heritage. Also, it is only in the East that Islam has been strongly rejected and Christianity wholesomely embraced to coexist with the ancestral belief systems of the people. The East is Nigeria’s exclusive Christendom. These commonalities, however, have failed to unite the people because of petty-mindedness and self-destructive rivalries stoked by external predators. Before the white man came, the hinterland traded and prospered with the coastal people. Despite being Igbo, my Abiriba cultural outlook is more of the riverine fashion. If you come to Abiriba, you will hear names derived from Bonny (Ubani), such as Jombo, Igbani and others. You will also hear names from the Calabar flank, such as Bassey, Erem (Edem), Itum, Okon, Asibong, and so on. My father’s name is Okpan, which is the same as Akpan (Efik/Ibibio). Yet, we, the Bende Igbo, are Igbo till the last man standing. Towards independence, the regionalisation of government awakened ethnic consciousness among the new educated elites who sought to position their peoples to ensure they were not disadvantaged under indigenous rule. That was when groups started aggregating into Igbo, Efik, Ibibio, Ijo, Ogoni and others. The main watershed of division in the former Eastern Region was the Biafra War. After the first coup of 15th January 1966, the North wanted to secede from Nigeria. If that had happened, all of us would have been in a much better world. But evil Britain, with their eyes on the rising oil wealth of the Eastern Region, installed Col. Yakubu Gowon as Nigeria’s Head of State. They gave him the “divide-and-rule” blueprint which they used to govern the British Empire, the largest empire in human history. The strategy was simple. To take full control of the oil resources of the Eastern Region, simply separate the Igbo from their Minority neighbours, thereby weakening both sides. Go into the Igbo dialectal groups in the Greater Port Harcourt areas and splinter them into “ethnic nationalities”. Hedge the main Igbo body into a small enclave and cut them off from the sea. To remove Ndi Igbo from Port Harcourt, declare the properties which they left behind during the War as “Abandoned Property” and share them among prominent Rivers State leaders. Tell the Ijo people that Rivers State is their war booty. While they trade hatred and fight, you sneak behind them and possess and plunder the oil and gas. If they agitate too much, you hang the leadership of the troublemakers and appoint a few “warlords” as pipeline guards (“maigads”). It worked like magic. Igbo groups in Rivers State started rewriting their oral histories, renaming their communities and inventing untenable tales of Benin origin bereft of Benin language, culture and names. Meanwhile, barefaced evidence points uncompromisingly to Igbo origins as validated by eminent colonial historiographers. Ask any AI platform about the ethnological origins of these self-denying groups. The answer is unequivocally, “Igboid”. Igbo denial has become a self-inflicted mental disease. A mentally deranged person is usually the last to know he is not well. I strongly believe that this matter should be settled through a scientific process: DNA checks. Any Igbo-speaking community that denies Igbo origin should undergo mass DNA tests. If Benin origin is confirmed, the argument is closed in favour of Benin heritage. I bet you, many of them will reject this option, choosing, instead, to remain the mosquito on the scrotum of the Igbo nation because they are on the payroll of the enemies of Igbo and Eastern unity. These enemies include the oil-well owners from faraway parts of Nigeria and the jihadists whose life ambition is to roll the East into the sack of the Fulani Caliphate and enslave the people as they have done to the Hausa. These Igbo deniers are threats to us. The post Igbo identity crisis: The DNA option (2), by Ochereome Nnanna appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Pakistan, Lebanon to boost security cooperation
items.description: Mohsin Naqvi welcomes his Lebanese counterpart Ahmad AI-Hajjar at the Ministry of Interior.—PPI • Dar reaffirms Pakistan’s support for Lebanon’s sovereignty • DPM, Grossi discuss regional situation, Islamabad MoU • Programme for upcoming UNGA session reviewed ISLAMABAD: Federal Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and his Lebanese counterpart, Ahmed Al-Hajjar, on Tuesday agreed to enhance cooperation in security, counterterrorism, anti-narcotics efforts, illegal immigration, money laundering, and cybercrime prevention. The two ministers held a one-on-one meeting, followed by delegation-level talks. They discussed ways to promote collaboration between police academies and training programmes, the regional situation, and Pakistan’s efforts to promote sustainable peace in the region. It was decided that an MoU would soon be signed to promote mutual cooperation between the two interior ministries. Both sides agreed to share intelligence to effectively combat terrorism, drug trafficking, and emerging security challenges. They also decided to fully implement the existing anti-narcotics MoU. They reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening bilateral ties. They also discussed providing visa-free entry facilities for holders of diplomatic and official passports between the two countries. Also, Lebanese Interior Minister Ahmad Al-Hajjar called on Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar and discussed bilateral cooperation. Mr Dar reaffirmed Pakistan’s support for Lebanon’s sovereignty. Meanwhile, DPM Dar discussed with Ambassador Rafael Grossi, Director General of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) and a candidate for UN Secretary-General the evolving regional situation and agreed that the implementation of the Islamabad MoU remained the best course of action to defuse regional tensions. Ambassador Grossi offered technical support should the need arise. Also, DPM Ishaq Dar chaired a meeting on Tuesday to review the programme for the upcoming 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly. The foreign secretary and UN special secretary briefed the deputy PM on the proposed programme, including high-level engagements, bilateral meetings, and other key engagements on the sidelines of the UNGA session. Published in Dawn, September 16th, 2026

items.title: All support acts on Ed Sheeran’s US tour quit after Macklemore dropped
items.description: All of the remaining support acts on Ed Sheeran’s US tour have quit after the rapper Macklemore was dropped from the line-up for making pro-Palestinian remarks on stage. Among them were Finneas, the brother of pop star Billie Eilish, who said in a statement: “Artists must not be silenced when they speak up for the oppressed.” Irish singer-songwriter Aaron Rowe and Danish band Lukas Graham also announced their departure. Irish folk band Beoga, who perform with Sheeran on stage every night, dropped out too. The announcements came hours after Sheeran said he would not be drawn into a public debate over Gaza, and stressed he was not responsible for Macklemore being removed from the tour. “Macklemore coming off tour was the promoter’s decision, it was not mine,” Sheeran said on Instagram. “I would never let down the fans who had made plans, nor would I abandon the touring crew and the other support acts and musicians who rely on me for work and to make a living.” Earlier this month, Macklemore – real name Benjamin Haggerty – called for a “free Palestine” and showed images of devastation in Gaza during two concerts in New Jersey. His comments drew criticism from Jewish groups, after which some venues put pressure on the tour promoters to drop him from the tour. In his statement , Sheeran said he had spoken with the venues “at length all week to try and build a bridge” – but the promoters, Messina Touring Group, had ultimately pulled the plug. Ed Sheeran and Macklemore, pictured in 2014, have been friends for 13 years, the rapper said in his statement on Monday While the star said he was “appalled by the conflict between Israel and Palestine” and that the “suffering and pain caused on both sides is a human tragedy”, he also attempted to explain his decision to keep political issues at arm’s length. “I am not complicit,” he wrote. “I have my personal views on this devastating conflict. Just because I choose not to speak publicly, it doesn’t mean I don’t have them, and it doesn’t mean I don’t care. “Nor does it mean I don’t support causes in my own, personal way.” He continued: “There is a reason I do not use my professional platform for politics – my audience includes young people, often children, of all backgrounds. “Those who come to my shows do not expect a political forum. I respect Macklemore’s strength of purpose to stand up and shout for what he believes. “However, there is room for multiple approaches to the same end: Peace. “I choose to use my fame and platform to be a place of safety and sanctuary, to maintain diplomacy and keep conversations open, not closed. If we only focus on shouting the loudest, nothing will ever change. There are different approaches to being an advocate for change.” Sheeran added that, “as with all my support acts”, Macklemore had been allowed to choose his own setlist. If the statement was meant to placate his fans and other artists on the line-up, it has seemingly had the opposite effect. Writing on Instagram, Lukas Graham said: “We should be able to speak about war, about civilians being killed, about children who deserve to grow up. Wherever they live. Whatever flag flies over them.” Rowe, who opened on the Australian leg of the tour earlier this year and resumed as a support act for the US in June, said that he did not “take the decision [to quit] lightly,” adding: “Ed has been a friend to me and has changed my life, I could never thank him enough for this.” In their post, Beoga said: “As musicians, playing to those crowds every night is the stuff of dreams but to play in venues that silence anyone advocating for a Free Palestine is simply not an option for us.” Hind’s Hall performance The controversy began on 4 September, when Macklemore performed at Ed Sheeran’s concert at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. He told the audience: “A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so that I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very, very dear to my heart: Free Palestine.” He then performed his song Hind’s Hall, which is dedicated to pro-Palestinian protestors at Columbia University and condemns Israel’s military action in Gaza, while video footage of the devastation in Gaza was shown on the big screen. Some of the audience cheered – but there was almost immediate criticism online. The Israeli American Council launched a petition demanding his removal from the tour; while the campaign group StopAntisemitism said the musician had ambushed fans with propaganda – a claim that was amplified by the pop star Pink, who reposted it on Instagram. The next night, Macklemore returned to the same stage and directly addressed his “Jewish brothers and sisters” in the audience. “Criticism of Israel, criticism of apartheid, being against genocide, is in no way a criticism of you,” he said, adding that he wanted people in Gaza and the West Bank to know they had not been forgotten. Israel rejects allegations of genocide. It says its troops conduct self-defence operations in Gaza and the occupied West Bank in accordance with international law. The Israeli military launched a campaign in Gaza in response to an unprecedented Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, in which about 1,200 people were killed, and 251 were taken hostage. During Israel’s military campaign in Gaza, more than 73,780 people have been killed, according to the territory’s Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN. ‘Most successful tour’ After days of press coverage, Macklemore announced on Monday that he had been dropped from the line-up. In a statement on Instagram, he said the boycott had been organised by Robert Kraft – the billionaire owner of Gillette Stadium in Massachusetts. Kraft – who once hired Ed Sheeran to play at his wedding – confirmed he’d made the decision to bar Macklemore, saying his venue would not “provide a platform for hate speech,” accusing the rapper of “a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric”. “I agree with Macklemore, too many lives have been lost, and there has been too much suffering, but only sharing selective information and ignoring the actions of Hamas is not honest and only advances more divisiveness and hate,” Kraft said. However, he did not address the claim that he’d asked other venues to put pressure on the tour. Tour promoter Messina Touring Group told Rolling Stone magazine that it had been told by venues that they would not allow Macklemore to perform, “which would result in the cancellation of the tour and impact hundreds of thousands of fans.” Many of the acts who withdrew on Tuesday night said Kraft’s involvement had influenced their decision. “Money doesn’t give you the right to own the conversation,” said Lukas Graham. “Nobody’s bank balance should decide who gets to speak or which suffering we’re allowed to acknowledge.” In his statement, Macklemore said he empathised with the difficult position Sheeran had been put in, but criticised the English singer for not taking a stance. “Taking a side can cost you. Money, brand deals, sponsorships, festivals, private shows, relationships and access. I’ve lost all of those things. But there is no neutral position between the oppressor and the oppressed,” he wrote. He also emphasised that, although he was only able to complete two shows on the tour, if his words succeeded in “turning the conversation back to Palestine, then it was the most successful tour I’ve ever been on.”

items.title: IHC allows Afghan doctor to continue post-grad training
items.description: ISLAMABAD / QUETTA: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Tuesday suspended an expulsion order against Afghan national Dr Imadud Din, halted his deportation from Pakistan and directed that he be allowed to continue his postgraduate medical training. IHC Justice Khadim Hussain Soomro granted the interim relief while hearing a constitutional petition filed by Dr Imadud Din’s wife, Mehar Zahoor, a Pakistani citizen, who challenged a notification issued by the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) seeking the repatriation of Afghan students enrolled in medical and dental institutions. During the hearing, the petitioner’s counsel, Barrister Qasim Nawaz Abbasi, argued that the PMDC communication dated July 31, 2026, could not be applied retrospectively to doctors already undergoing training. He contended that the petitioner’s husband was not a fresh applicant but an already enrolled trainee in the fifth year of his FCPS-II training in urology at Quaid-i-Azam Medical College (QAMC) and Bahawal Victoria Hospital (BVH), Bahawalpur. BHC dismisses petitions by Afghan medical students; notes they don’t have absolute right to remain, study in Pakistan The counsel informed the court that the competent authority at QAMC, on the recommendation of the head of department, had formally granted Dr Imadud Din an extension in his postgraduate training from Feb 28, 2026, to Feb 27, 2027. Barrister Abbasi argued that the impugned communication directed institutions to initiate measures for the repatriation of Afghan students, a move that would cause irreparable professional and financial loss to the petitioner’s family, which included two children. He maintained that while the petitioner did not object to future policies regulating admissions, trainees already enrolled and those granted extensions should be permitted to complete their training. The counsel emphasised that terminating Dr Imadud Din’s training without prior notice or a meaningful opportunity of hearing violated constitutional guarantees under Articles 4, 9, 10-A, 14 and 35. After hearing the arguments, Justice Soomro suspended the operation of the impugned communication to the extent of its application to Dr Imadud Din and restrained the respondents from terminating, discontinuing or obstructing his ongoing postgraduate training solely based on the PMDC letter. The court adjourned the proceedings and issued notices to the secretary of the Ministry of National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination, the president and registrar of the PMDC, the principal of Quaid-i-Azam Medical College, and the secretary of Punjab’s Specialised Healthcare and Medical Education Department, seeking their responses. BHC dismisses pleas Meanwhile, the Balochistan High Court on Tuesday dismissed constitutional petitions seeking permission for Afghan nationals to continue medical and dental education, as well as postgraduate training, in Pakistan. A two-member bench comprising Justice Muhammad Aamir Nawaz Rana and Justice Abdul Qayyum Lehri announced the verdict on two petitions filed by Afghan students, upholding the state policy concerning the stay and education of foreign nationals in Pakistan. The court held that foreign nationals did not have an absolute or permanent right to remain, study or undergo professional training in Pakistan in a manner contrary to state policy. The bench also declined to interfere with directions issued by the PMDC concerning the admission, transfer and facilitation of Afghan nationals in medical institutions. The court observed that matters relating to immigration, the return of foreign nationals and national security primarily fell within the domain of the executive authorities. However, it stressed that Afghan nationals must be treated with human dignity and fairness and in accordance with the law. The petitions were dismissed at the preliminary stage. Published in Dawn, September 16th, 2026

items.title: Education as common Northern responsibility: From 19 separate efforts to 1 Northern compact (2), by Usman Sarki
items.description: “The strength of a race is found both in material and spiritual things associated with that race, that form the kernel of its being and progress or, alternatively, its degeneration.” — John Buchan When material and spiritual advance cease and degeneration becomes the norm, the perdition of a race or society becomes inevitable. The argument advanced in the first part of this article was straightforward: Northern Nigeria’s education emergency has become too profound and interconnected to be approached exclusively through nineteen separate state programmes. The historical experience of the Interim Common Services Agency (ICSA) demonstrated that the successor states of the former Northern Region once recognised an important principle: certain interests were better preserved and certain services better delivered collectively. The challenge today is not to recreate ICSA but to rediscover its philosophy and apply it creatively to twenty-first-century realities. If education is accepted as a common Northern challenge, what precisely should be done? The first requirement is political acknowledgement. The nineteen Northern governors should collectively declare education a regional human-capital emergency and establish a Northern States Education and Human Capital Compact. Such a declaration should contain measurable obligations undertaken by each state and collective obligations undertaken by all. A small professional coordinating institution, perhaps a Northern States Council on Education and Human Capital Development, could support it. It need not become another costly bureaucracy. Its purpose should be coordination, data collection, standard setting, common programmes, resource mobilisation, benchmarking and independent assessment. Its governing body could include representatives of the Northern Governors’ Forum, commissioners of education, universities and colleges of education, traditional institutions, religious scholars, business leaders, women’s organisations and recognised education specialists. Its success, however, should be judged by results rather than meetings. The first practical task must be to determine accurately the scale of the problem. Northern Nigeria needs a comprehensive Education Census and Human Capital Map. We need not wait for the Federal Government to provide this service. We should know, settlement by settlement, how many children are of school age; how many attend school; how many do not; how many teachers exist; what subjects they teach; the condition of school infrastructure; gender disparities; disability requirements; security challenges; and the reasons children remain outside formal education. This exercise is within our capacity, especially with the involvement of traditional rulers and community institutions. Without reliable information, policy becomes little more than speculation or spectacle. The second objective should be bold enough to capture public imagination: “Every Northern Child Learning by 2030”, coinciding with the terminal date of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. The objective must not simply be enrolment. Putting children into classrooms without ensuring that they learn merely converts an access problem into a quality problem. Every child completing basic education should possess functional literacy, numeracy, digital familiarity, civic knowledge, communication skills and either preparation for higher education or an identifiable vocational pathway. The third priority is teachers. No educational transformation can occur without competent and motivated teachers. Instead of nineteen largely isolated and under-resourced teacher-development systems, selected institutions across the North could become specialised regional centres. One might concentrate on training mathematics and science teachers; another on technical and vocational education; another on early-childhood education; another on special-needs teaching; and another on school leadership and administration. Northern states could jointly finance accelerated teacher training and continuous professional development. We should question the rationale for every state attempting to become self-sufficient in every specialised field when expertise can be shared and resources pooled. The fourth priority must address Qur’anic, Almajiri and nomadic education with greater intellectual seriousness than has often characterised public debate. For centuries, Qur’anic schooling formed an important part of Northern Muslim society. The challenge is not religious education itself. The difficulty arises where children receive religious instruction without acquiring the additional knowledge and skills required to function effectively in contemporary society. A new Northern compact could therefore develop agreed minimum learning standards through consultation with respected Islamic scholars, traditional authorities and education specialists. A child attending Qur’anic education should simultaneously acquire literacy, mathematics, basic science, civic knowledge and practical skills where appropriate. Rather than destroying an established institution, policy should modernise, strengthen and give it more respectability and relevance. The fifth priority must be girls’ education. No society can develop successfully while substantially under-investing in half its population. The issue should be framed not as an imported cultural argument driven by instruments like CEDAW, but as a Northern development necessity. An educated woman contributes directly to household income, child health, social stability, the educational attainment of subsequent generations and broader economic productivity. Traditional rulers, Islamic scholars, Christian leaders, women’s organisations and community leaders should therefore become active participants in a renewed campaign for girls’ education across the region. The sixth priority should be technical and vocational education. For too long, education in Nigeria has been conceptualised overwhelmingly as a pathway from primary school to secondary school, university and government employment, emphasising certification more than qualification. That model cannot absorb the enormous youth population now emerging. Northern Nigeria urgently requires technicians, electricians, irrigation specialists, welders, builders, tilers, painters, machinists, mechanics, solar installers, agricultural technicians, mobile-phone and computer repairers, veterinary assistants, ICT workers, leather processors and hundreds of other skilled occupations. Every senatorial district should have access to high-quality vocational and apprenticeship opportunities connected directly to local economic activity. Education must be linked to production. In Kano, this may mean textiles, leather, ironwork, manufacturing and commerce. In Borno and Yobe, agriculture, livestock, irrigation, solar energy and cross-border trade may receive particular emphasis. In Plateau, Nasarawa and Niger, mining, agriculture and processing may feature more strongly. Educational planning should reflect economic geography. The seventh area for common action is technology. A Northern digital learning platform could make high-quality lessons available across participating states at reasonable cost. Excellent teachers need not be confined physically to individual classrooms. Lessons in mathematics, chemistry, physics, English and technical subjects can be recorded, transmitted and shared. Solar-powered digital facilities could also assist schools where electricity remains unreliable. The eighth requirement is financing. Education must cease to be treated as residual expenditure after prestige projects such as airports and flyovers have been funded. Northern governments must commit greater and more efficiently managed resources to basic education. Collective action also creates new opportunities. Nineteen states acting together could develop major programmes with the Federal Government, the World Bank, the African Development Bank, the Islamic Development Bank, UNICEF, UNESCO, Education Cannot Wait and other development partners. Scale therefore matters. A programme involving several million children across a vast region, supported by reliable data and nineteen state governments, would possess considerably greater strategic weight than fragmented projects submitted independently by individual states. The ninth requirement is accountability. Every year, an independent State of Northern Education Report should be published. Each state should be assessed against agreed indicators, including enrolment, attendance, completion, literacy, numeracy, teacher quality, gender parity, infrastructure and vocational transition. The results should be made public. Healthy competition could then emerge. Instead of governors competing principally over flyovers, airports and government buildings, Kano could compete with Kaduna over literacy; Jigawa with Bauchi over school completion; Borno with Yobe over girls’ enrolment; Niger with Plateau over technical education; Kwara with Kogi over nomadic schools, etc. Such competition would be far more consequential to the region’s future. This brings us directly to 2027. Education should become an electoral test. The Northern Elders Forum, Arewa Consultative Forum, the League of Northern Democrats and other civic organisations could invite presidential and governorship candidates to endorse a Northern Education and Human Capital Charter. Candidates should be asked for measurable commitments rather than rhetoric: What will you do during your first year? How many additional children will enter school? How many teachers will be recruited and trained? How will insecurity around schools be addressed? How will religious education be integrated? How will technical education be expanded? What proportion of the budget will be devoted to education? And will you support a common institutional framework among the nineteen Northern states? What are your plans for nomadic education? These questions should be asked repeatedly throughout the campaign. Indeed, one of the most consequential presidential or Northern gubernatorial debates of the 2027 election season could be devoted entirely to education. Not to roads, contracts, offices or political appointments, but to our children, our human capital and our posterity. For Northern Nigeria, that is no longer merely an educational question. It is a question of survival and, as John Buchan noted, that forms the kernel of progress or degeneration. The choice is ours: whether to advance or to degenerate. The post Education as common Northern responsibility: From 19 separate efforts to 1 Northern compact (2), by Usman Sarki appeared first on Vanguard News .
