items.title: GB unveils Rs218.8bn budget after long wait
items.description: GILGIT: The Gilgit-Baltistan government on Tue­s­day presented a three-month delayed budget of Rs218.845 billion for fiscal year 2026-27, with a deficit of over Rs52bn, seeking additional funds from the federal government to meet various liabilities. It may be mentioned here that in July, the GB government had presen­ted a Rs20.478bn interim budget for the first quarter of FY27 and announced that the full-year budget would be presented after three months. Senior Minister Moham­mad Ali Akhtar, who also holds the finance portfolio, presented the budget in the GB Assembly on Tuesday, presided over by Speaker Imran Nadeem. He told the house that the elected government had assumed office at the end of June 2026. “Since only a very limited amount of time was available bet­w­een the end of the financial year and the beginning of the new financial year, the government had to ensure continuity of governmental affairs and the timely provision of essential expenditures.” Therefore, he said, a three-month interim budget for the initial three months of FY27 was presented on the basis of the previous financial year. “At that time, our government clearly preferred to take the necessary time rather than present a full-year budget, so that the annual budget would not merely be a collection of figures, but could truly reflect the genuine needs, priorities and aspirations of the people,” he added. Mr Akhtar said the budget was, placing special emphasis on education, health, basic infrastructure and the welfare of the underprivileged segment of society. He said the total budget was estimated at approximately Rs218.845bn, with Rs43.97bn allocated for development and Rs149.87bn for non-development expenditure. He said the volume of the GB budget reached Rs218bn when the federal government’s stabilisation package was included. He said tax revenues were targeted at Rs16.98bn, while efforts were under way to secure the required funds from the federal government to meet the budget deficit of Rs52.65bn. He said the size of ADP had been increased from Rs22bn to Rs23bn, while the amount allocated under the federal PSDP had been increased from Rs15bn to Rs20.973bn, including Rs4bn under PM’s package. The minister said the wheat subsidy fund that had been reduced to Rs15bn was raised to Rs22bn. The estimated revenue from wheat sale was Rs3bn, he added. He said GB had requested a special stabilisation package of around Rs153.30bn from the federal government for economic and administrative stability. “Under this package, targets have been set for the stability of local governments, law and order, education, health, tourism, compensation for flood losses, municipal services, food supply, e-governance, tourism, agriculture, climate change, institutional capacity building, and clearing various liabilities,” he said. The minister said the minimum wage for employees in all government and non-government institutions had been raised from Rs40,000 to Rs44,000. He said Rs63.57bn had been allocated for salaries, while Rs1.048bn had been set aside for education. “For the first time in history, Rs1bn has been allocated for social protection, and a proposal has been made to establish a Rs4bn endowment fund for the social sector,” he added. Mr Akhtar said climate funds were previously earmarked within development projects, but in practice, no actual deductions were being made for this purpose. For the first time, one per cent of development funds would be diverted to a consolidated account, he added. In light of climate change concerns, the GB government had decided to procure hybrid vehicles for government departments and auction off older vehicles that con­sumed excessive fuel, he said. The minister also ann­ounced that the non-development budgets of all departments were being reduced by 30pc. He said substantial funds had been allocated for improving the health, education and agriculture sectors. These included an increase of Rs170m for the procurement of medicines, and the establishment of a health endowment fund. He said Rs50m had been allocated for water management to promote the agriculture sector and Rs50m for agriculture sector reform initiatives. “Rs50m for loans for youth, Rs50m for local bodies elections and Rs50m for renovation of local bodies offices have been allocated. Rs78m has been allocated for water and power department and Rs18m for tourism department,” he said. For development projects in 10 districts, Rs5.034bn has been allocated. Earlier, a GB cabinet meeting approved the budget. Published in Dawn, September 16th, 2026

items.title: Ministers sound alarm as energy crunch looms
items.description: • Federal cabinet members insist prudent planning averted a worse crisis • PM’s fuel relief scheme set for nationwide rollout from midnight • Local resources kept lights on amid Hormuz disruption, says Leghari • Rs100 relief per litre is all economy can bear right now: Musadik • Govt denies ‘smart lockdown’ rumours as fuel costs spiral ISLAMABAD: With Gulf energy transit routes effectively closed and fuel prices spiralling , members of the federal cabinet on Tuesday sounded the alarm regarding the energy situation in the country — both in terms of fuel supplies and power generation — while maintaining that things could have been much worse, if not for prudent planning on the government’s part. Giving a rundown of the way disruptions in the Hormuz and Bab El-Mandeb straits could have exacerbated prevailing shortages, Energy Minister Sardar Awais Ahmad Khan Leghari and Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik highlighted how skyrocketing prices on the international oil market were testing the government’s ability to absorb such price shocks. Meanwhile, the National Steering Com­mittee on Fuel Subsidy — chaired by Deputy PM Ishaq Dar — ordered that payments to fuel stations under the PM’s sch­eme be processed within 24 hours, while directing provinces to complete dist­rict-level outreach to ensure seamless delivery of relief to the intended beneficiaries. According to an official statement, the meeting was held to review the nationwide rollout of the PM’s Fuel Relief Scheme, and noted that following a successful pilot in the capital, the scheme would be extended countrywide from midnight tonight, i.e. between Wedn­esday and Thursday. Absorbing price shocks Addressing a press conference in the capital, the climate change minister linked the recent increase in fuel prices to the upward movement in international crude oil prices, which had crossed the $100 per barrel threshold once again. The price of oil has not come down and the US/Israel-Iran war has not stopped, he said, adding that the government was seeking to absorb part of the external sho­ck to protect vulnerable segments of society, referring to the PM’s Fuel Relief Scheme. Under the scheme, motorcyclists would receive five litres of subsidised petrol every week, while car owners would be entitled to 10 litres every 10 days. The minister clarified that the petroleum levy was Rs80 per litre and the carbon levy Rs5, making a combined Rs85, while the relief announced under the scheme was Rs100 per litre. He conceded that the relief being provided was still insufficient to fully offset the impact of high fuel prices, but maintained that this burden was the most the national economy could currently absorb. Giving an example, Dr Musadik said delivery riders had been particularly affected by higher petrol prices as they continued to travel the same distances to deliver food and other goods while their fuel costs had increased substantially. He said a relief of Rs2,000 could make a significant difference to a low-income delivery riders household by helping meet basic expenses such as food, milk and eggs. The minister also cited the example of a woman who drives a Qingqi rickshaw to support her family. He said the Rs2,000 monthly fuel relief could help her meet her child’s school fee. Another beneficiary, drives an 800cc car to a factory while his wife uses the same vehicle to take their children to school. He would receive relief on up to 30 litres of petrol, amounting to Rs3,000 a month, he added. In a separate statement, the energy minister echoed his cabinet colleague’s warnings about the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, adding that despite fuel shortages, Pakistan was able to keep its power plants whirring thanks to maximum utilisation of domestic resources. In August 2026, 72 per cent of total electricity generation was sourced from domestic resources, including hydel (38pc), local coal (11pc), nuclear (10pc), local gas (7pc), wind (6pc) and solar energy (1pc), while only 28pc came from imported coal and RLNG, he said. Mr Leghari said that due to disruptions in the RLNG supply chain, spot cargo prices had risen to $23.25 per MMBtu, which was exceptionally high. In these circumstances, he said, steps taken on the PM’s directives to arrange additional domestic gas for the power sector made it possible to avoid purchasing expensive RLNG. If domestic gas had not been available, the power sector would have faced an additional hour of load shedding, he said. Moreover, generation through furnace oil or imported RLNG would have increased overall consumer tariffs by around Rs 10.6bn. Lockdown rumours Fuel prices continued to spiral, with both petrol and diesel witnessing Rs4 and Rs6 increase on Tuesday night. The series of steep increases over the past three days, taken together with Information Minister Atta Tarar’s hint that austerity measures may be reintroduced in view of the developing situation, sparked speculation about possible lockdown-style measures being imposed. However, both Musadik Malik and his cabinet colleague Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry brushed aside these reports, with the former insisting that no discussions about ‘smart lockdowns’ had taken place, and the latter flat out refuting all such speculation. The government had already imposed a similar smart lockdown in the country in April with the help of provincial governments when the US-Iran war started. During that period, shops and markets were closed at 8pm. Interestingly, sources close to PM Shahbaz told Dawn that the premier met his elder brother Nawaz Sharif at the Murree hill resort on Tuesday, with the possibility of imposing measures such as ‘smart lockdown’ being on the agenda. However, there was no official word on the meeting from PM Office or PML-N. Published in Dawn, September 16th, 2026

items.title: We have the greatest public finance scandal of 4th Republic – Dafeamekpor on COVID-19 audit
items.description: Majority Chief Whip and South Dayi MP Rockson-Nelson Dafeamekpor has called for immediate arrests if allegations of concealed findings in the Auditor-General’s COVID-19 expenditure audit are established. His comments follow investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni’s latest investigation, which raises questions over the Auditor-General’s special audit of COVID-19 spending. The investigation found that the Auditor-General’s report recorded GH¢96 million as COVID-19 fumigation expenditure, while documents examined by Manasseh indicate that government ministries spent hundreds of millions of cedis more on the exercise. The investigation specifically found that the Ministry of Local Government spent about GH¢299 million on three fumigation contracts, but that expenditure was not included in the Auditor-General’s reported fumigation figure. The Ghana Audit Service has confirmed that the expenditure was audited but has not explained why it was omitted from the figure reported. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, Dafeamekpor said the allegations, if proven, could amount to an unprecedented public finance scandal. “If what Manasseh Azure Awuni is further revealing is what is actually the case, then arguably we have the greatest public finance scandal of maybe the Fourth Republic.” He said the Auditor-General has a legal obligation to report the findings of a special audit to Parliament. “You cannot conceal any facts from Parliament.” Dafeamekpor argued that the evidence presented by Manasseh indicates the audit was conducted, but that material findings and recommendations were omitted from the report submitted to Parliament. “So where the evidence, the pieces of material evidence that he’s pieced together, points irresistibly to the fact that they actually conducted the audit of the Ministry of Local Government and Transport, but in reporting to Parliament, concealed material findings and perhaps recommendations for consideration by Parliament and perhaps leading to legislative reforms from Parliament, they’re in breach of Section 16.” He said he was considering issuing a formal statement on the matter but insisted that the allegations required immediate action if confirmed. “So me, I’m really hesitating to issue the statement I’m minded to do.” Dafeamekpor then called for arrests. “If this is really the issue tonight, then people should be, the arrests should be happening before daybreak tomorrow, because this cannot be countenanced under any circumstances in this country.” The controversy centres on the findings of a special audit of COVID-19 expenditure commissioned in 2022. Manasseh’s investigation says the audit significantly understated fumigation expenditure across several ministries. Former Auditor-General Daniel Domelevo has separately said the discrepancy must be explained, warning that either information was withheld from auditors or the audit was not properly conducted.

Une rentrée qui intervient dans un contexte dominé par la crise sécuritaire dans l’est du pays, l’annonce d’un dialogue national pour la paix et les tensions autour de la loi sur le référendum. items.title: Govt raises petrol price by Rs4.10 per litre, HSD by Rs6.41 per litre
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · "> The government on Tuesday increased the price of petrol by Rs4.10 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs6.41 per litre. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs384.34 per litre while HSD will cost Rs415.83 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on Sept 16 (Wednesday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. A statement from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said owners of two- and three-wheelers would receive relief of Rs100 per litre on a monthly quota of 20 litres, while owners of vehicles up to 800cc would receive the same relief on a monthly quota of 30 litres. On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Xénophobie en Afrique du Sud: des réfugiés évacués de Durban vers le camp de Lindela, à 600 km
items.description: À Durban, en Afrique du Sud, après quatre mois à vivre dehors, devant un bâtiment gouvernemental, en plein hiver austral et dans des conditions indignes, les réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile de la rue Che Guevara ont été évacués. Tous ont été contrôlés par les services de l’immigration et disposent de documents en règle. Mais face aux violences et aux intimidations de manifestants xénophobes, beaucoup sont montés dans des bus affrétés par le gouvernement pour rejoindre un camp situé à 600 kilomètres de là, dans l’espoir d’y être protégés.

items.title: MAB International Hospital’s Akuamah-Boateng wins 10th anniversary Forty Under 40 Ghana Award
items.description: The Chief Executive Director of MAB International Hospital, Opare Akuamah-Boateng, has been named a winner at the 10th anniversary edition of the Forty Under 40 Ghana Awards. Mr Akuamah-Boateng was recognised for his leadership and contribution to the growth of MAB International Hospital, where he began his career as an Estate Manager before rising to become Chief Executive Director. The award was presented at a ceremony held at the Kempinski Gold Coast Hotel in Accra as part of activities marking the 10th anniversary of the Forty Under 40 Ghana Awards. The ceremony brought together award recipients, their families, and other stakeholders to celebrate young professionals and business leaders who have made contributions across various sectors. A total of 44 individuals received awards across different categories, while honorary awards were presented to 16 individuals for their contributions to the development of the awards scheme over the past decade. The Forty Under 40 Ghana Awards is an annual initiative established to recognise professionals, entrepreneurs, business leaders and other individuals under the age of 40 who are making an impact in their respective fields. The awards cover sectors including banking and finance, energy, agriculture, technology, family business, fashion, media and social enterprise. The ceremony also saw the Chief Executive Officer of Premier EL Consult, Dr Marian Bokor, receive the People’s Choice Award. Chief Executive Officer of Xodus Communications Limited and founder of the Forty Under 40 Awards, Richard Abbey Jnr, described the 10-year journey as a significant milestone for the initiative. He said the awards had provided a platform for identifying and celebrating young talents while encouraging them to develop their leadership and entrepreneurial potential. “Forty Under Forty is value-driven and process-focused, and we are proud to give this huge platform for many people to launch their potential,” he said. Mr Abbey said the achievements and ideas of award recipients over the years offered opportunities for young professionals to contribute to addressing some of Ghana’s development challenges. He said the initiative had also expanded beyond Ghana through Forty Under 40 Africa and Forty Under 40 Global, with programmes extending to countries including South Africa, the United Kingdom and the United States. According to him, the initiative now has more than 600 alumni, about 200 winners and has spotlighted more than 2,000 nominees. Looking ahead, Mr Abbey said the organisation was seeking International Organisation for Standardisation (ISO) certification within the next decade and was also working towards a franchise model that could allow other countries to operate the initiative. Board Chairman of Forty Under 40, Prof David Atta-Peters, said the initiative had established a network of young professionals and entrepreneurs over the past decade. He urged award recipients to continue demonstrating leadership and innovation in their respective fields. Prof Atta-Peters also encouraged young people to pursue entrepreneurship and develop solutions to national development challenges. Meanwhile, Chief Executive Officer of KAB-FAM Ghana Ltd, Charles Antwi-Boahen, called on young entrepreneurs and business leaders to embrace technology and innovation as the business environment evolves. He said the growing use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and other technologies meant businesses needed to adapt their operations to remain competitive. Mr Antwi-Boahen said technology could help businesses overcome operational barriers and create opportunities for Ghanaian entrepreneurs to connect with markets across Africa and beyond.

items.title: Libye: près de 100 000 pilules d’ecstasy à l’effigie de Mouammar Kadhafi saisies
items.description: C’est une drôle de manière pour le colonel Kadhafi de faire son retour en Libye. L’ancien dirigeant apparaît sculpté sur des milliers de pilules d’ecstasy d’une cargaison saisie, dimanche 13 septembre 2026, par les autorités libyennes. Les images diffusées par les services de sécurité à Tripoli montrent des comprimés marqués du visage de Mouammar Kadhafi et moulés à l’image de sa tête et de ses épaules, avec les traits distinctifs de son visage et de ses vêtements imprimés à leur surface. items.title: Rubio announces US visa curbs for some foreign nationals from South Africa
items.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Tuesday that the U.S. was announcing a new visa restriction policy targeting some foreign nationals from South Africa, as President Donald Trump’s administration continues to cool ties with the country. The Trump administration has criticised South Africa over a range of issues, including actions aimed at addressing racial inequality that Trump claims hurt ​the African nation’s white population. Washington has also criticised land reform policies and South ​Africa’s genocide case against Israel at the International Court of Justice, over the U.S. ⁠ally’s assault on Gaza . The visa curb policy targets “foreign nationals who are responsible for, or ​complicit in, the enactment or implementation of laws or policies that enable uncompensated land seizures, ​race-based discrimination, and/or the incitement of imminent violence against members of minority ethnic or racial groups in South Africa,” Rubio said in a statement. “The South African government has not adequately addressed the previously laid ​out concerns,” Rubio said. The South African embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to a ​request for comment. Pretoria says there is no evidence of discrimination or persecution against white people and that ‌ideas ⁠of white racial superiority are a threat to South Africa’s post-apartheid unity, its sovereignty and its diplomatic relations. President Cyril Ramaphosa has called for global efforts to debunk false stories about white persecution. Trump has previously cut aid to South Africa , offered refuge to white minority Afrikaners, expelled ​the country’s ambassador and ​made false claims of ⁠white genocide in the African nation. Trump’s portrayal of South Africa as dangerous and oppressive for white people also aligns with some of ​his domestic policies that have targeted diversity initiatives aimed at addressing ​historic inequities for ⁠marginalised groups. Trump casts them as discriminatory against white people and men. Rubio’s statement on Tuesday did not name any person. Three decades after the end of apartheid in South Africa, ⁠some ​fringe groups lament the loss of white power that ​democracy brought. While South Africa has one of the highest murder rates in the world, most victims are Black.

items.title: Fête de l’indépendance : l’AGUIPE-E lance une formation en faveur de 1 300 jeunes
items.description: À l’occasion de la célébration du 68ᵉ anniversaire de l’indépendance de la Guinée, l’Agence guinéenne pour la promotion de l’emploi et de l’entrepreneuriat (AGUIPE-E) a lancé, ce mardi 15 septembre 2026, un programme de formation destiné aux jeunes à travers le pays. Portée par le ministère de l’Emploi, du Travail et de la Protection sociale à travers l’AGUIPE-E, cette initiative vise à renforcer les compétences des jeunes et à améliorer leur employabilité. La cérémonie de lancement a été présidée par la secrétaire générale du ministère de l’Emploi, du Travail et de la Protection sociale, Ramatoulaye Camara. Placée au cœur de l’action des autorités, la valorisation du capital humain constitue l’un des axes mis en avant par le département. C’est dans cette dynamique que s’inscrit ce programme de formation, selon le directeur général de l’AGUIPE-E, Antighou Chérif. « La formation que nous lançons aujourd’hui n’est donc pas une activité isolée. Elle marque le début d’une mobilisation qui se poursuivra jusqu’à la semaine de l’Indépendance et qui s’étendra à plusieurs localités du territoire national. De Conakry à Kindia et Mamou, puis à Boké, Kankan, N’Zérékoré, Labé, Faranah, Kissidougou et Kouroussa, nos équipes iront à la rencontre des demandeurs d’emploi à travers des formations, des caravanes de l’emploi et de l’entrepreneuriat, mais également des actions de prospection auprès des entreprises et de mise en relation avec les opportunités disponibles », a-t-il déclaré. Selon lui, l’objectif est de toucher près de 1 200 bénéficiaires d’ici au 2 octobre 2026, à travers des formations en techniques de recherche d’emploi, en entrepreneuriat, des formations qualifiantes et des master class. S’adressant aux jeunes bénéficiaires, Antighou Chérif les a invités à prendre au sérieux les différents modules proposés, estimant que leur implication est essentielle pour mieux valoriser leurs compétences sur le marché de l’emploi. « Chers demandeurs d’emploi et jeunes, le message de l’AGUIPE-E aujourd’hui est simple : une opportunité devient réellement utile lorsqu’on est préparé à la saisir. Notre responsabilité est de vous accompagner, de vous orienter, de vous former et de rapprocher de vous les opportunités. Mais l’opportunité ou la chance seule ne suffit pas. Votre réussite dépendra de votre implication, de votre discipline, de votre capacité à écouter, à apprendre et à appliquer », a-t-il souligné. Il les a également encouragés à participer activement aux séances de formation. « Suivez cette formation avec attention ; posez des questions ; participez activement : testez, corrigez, améliorez-vous. Ce qui permettra de vous rapprocher de ces opportunités et de les saisir. Comme je l’ai dit plus haut, cette formation n’est pas une formation isolée. Nous voulons surtout que cette dynamique se poursuive au-delà du 2 octobre. Car célébrer l’Indépendance, c’est aussi préparer une jeunesse capable de travailler, d’entreprendre et de prendre pleinement sa place dans la transformation économique de la Guinée », a ajouté le directeur général de l’AGUIPE-E. Ramatoulaye Camara : « Construire l’avenir de la Guinée, c’est nécessairement préparer sa jeunesse » Prenant la parole, la secrétaire générale du ministère de l’Emploi, du Travail et de la Protection sociale a salué cette initiative, qu’elle estime en adéquation avec les orientations des autorités en matière de développement du capital humain et de transformation économique, notamment à travers le programme Simandou 2040. Pour Ramatoulaye Camara, le thème de cette célébration, « S’inspirer du passé pour construire ensemble l’avenir », revêt une importance particulière. « Ce choix est particulièrement significatif. Car construire l’avenir de la Guinée, c’est nécessairement préparer sa jeunesse à prendre toute sa place dans la transformation économique et sociale de notre pays », a-t-elle déclaré. Elle a également rappelé que la valorisation du capital humain, la jeunesse et la participation des Guinéens à la transformation économique du pays occupent une place importante dans l’action publique. « Nous voulons donc exprimer notre reconnaissance au Président de la République pour cette orientation qui nous rappelle une exigence essentielle : les transformations économiques que connaît aujourd’hui notre pays doivent produire des opportunités concrètes pour les Guinéennes et les Guinéens », a-t-elle poursuivi. Selon elle, le programme Simandou 2040 constitue une traduction de cette ambition à long terme. « Les infrastructures, les investissements et les grands projets n’auront pleinement de sens que s’ils permettent parallèlement de développer les compétences nationales, de créer des emplois, de faire émerger des entrepreneurs guinéens et de préparer notre jeunesse aux métiers dont la Guinée aura besoin demain. C’est précisément dans cet esprit que s’inscrivent les formations que nous lançons aujourd’hui », a laissé entendre Ramatoulaye Camara. Les jeunes bénéficiaires affichent leurs attentes Ils sont nombreux, jeunes hommes et femmes, à prendre part à ces séances de formation. Conscients des défis qui les attendent, ils souhaitent renforcer leurs compétences et mieux se préparer à leur insertion professionnelle. Après avoir salué l’initiative, Bintou Camara, Fatoumata Barry et Sory Kourouma, respectivement diplômées en comptabilité, en banque et finance et titulaire d’un Master of Business Administration (MBA), ont exprimé leurs attentes. « J’apprécie vraiment cette initiative parce qu’elle nous aide, nous les jeunes, à nous former et à mieux nous préparer au marché de l’emploi », témoigne l’une des participantes. Une autre estime que l’initiative intervient dans un contexte marqué par les difficultés d’accès à l’emploi : « C’est vraiment un travail à féliciter. Ils fournissent beaucoup d’efforts pour nous, les jeunes, surtout dans un contexte où l’accès à l’emploi est actuellement très compliqué. » Pour Sory Kourouma, cette formation devrait notamment permettre d’améliorer ses connaissances en recherche d’emploi et en entrepreneuriat. « Mes attentes vis-à-vis de cette formation sont, entre autres, de sortir mieux outillé en matière de techniques de recherche d’emploi et d’acquérir davantage de connaissances et de compétences dans le domaine de l’entrepreneuriat », a-t-il indiqué. Le ministère de l’Emploi, du Travail et de la Protection sociale, à travers l’AGUIPE-E, entend multiplier ce type d’initiatives au-delà de la célébration de la fête de l’indépendance, prévue le 2 octobre prochain. L’objectif affiché est de contribuer à renforcer l’employabilité des jeunes Guinéens et à leur permettre de mieux répondre aux exigences d’un marché du travail en constante évolution. items.title: 2027: Let us end this presidential campaign charade
items.description: By SUNNY IKHIOYA It is not a matter of whether you love President Bola Tinubu or not. It is a question of the way forward for Nigeria. We are taught to believe that politics is a contest of ideas. The side that convinces the people that it has the best way forward wins. This is because there is no unidirectional path to governance. As economists would put it, there is always “the other hand.” That is why a strong opposition is a sine qua non in every political system, no matter the ideology in place. The government of President Goodluck Jonathan exemplified this by giving opposition parties the freedom to express themselves in any manner they chose. They called him all kinds of names and even went to the extent of carrying a coffin to signify his death. But all Jonathan said was, “No blood must be shed on my behalf.” That was real democracy at work: freedom of speech, movement and association. But all of this became an illusion immediately after a very vibrant opposition took over government. It is becoming clear that those who rode to power on the crest of populism ended up becoming dictators once they assumed power. We saw it with Kabila of the DRC. We have seen it with Yoweri Museveni of Uganda. And we are seeing it with the APC government in Nigeria. What do they have in common? Intolerance of opposition. But the opposition in Nigeria has also shot itself in the foot in the manner in which it is challenging for the ultimate political prize: the presidency. It has become so desperate that it has thrown all caution to the wind. It is concentrating on destroying the person of President Bola Tinubu instead of providing intelligent and winnable strategies to unseat the government. And I believe this will not lead it anywhere. The 2027 presidential election, at this rate, is as good as done and dusted. The opposition will not like to hear this, but it is the truth. Its capacity has been seriously degraded by its pursuit of inanities. It is going after Tinubu’s Chicago certificate, an issue that has been in the Nigerian public space since Gani Fawehinmi took him to court on October 7, 1999. That was 27 years ago. Since then, the man went on to serve two terms as governor and performed creditably. He also became the arrowhead of Lagos State politics and rallied a national coalition to defeat an incumbent president in the 2015 elections. All this while, those bent on destroying him now were his close friends and confidants. He used his platform — the Action Congress — to support Atiku in his failed 2007 election bid. This man was the acclaimed leader of the APC even when he was not in government, and nobody questioned his competence and qualifications then. He became president despite serious opposition from within and outside his party, with the Chicago certificate scandal at the forefront of the campaign. The matter even went as far as the Supreme Court to determine his eligibility, and he won. In a country where the court has ruled that you do not need a school certificate to become president, dragging a certificate matter for eternity smacks of extreme jealousy and wickedness. What you could not do while the man was not even in government, you now want to do. Someone said, “Tinubu is not Jonathan,” and I agree. Tinubu is not unbeatable if the right strategies are adopted. But are we using the right strategies? Is it right to over-rely on a strategy that has been in the public space since 1999, when Gani took him to court over the Chicago certificate matter? Have we factored in our cultural and religious dynamics to conclude that these strategies will work? Have fellow Nigerians suffered enough to collectively decide that the suffering must be put to an end? Have the masses been educated and enlightened enough to discern when they are being taken for a ride? Are our opposition politicians patriotic enough to put their personal ambitions aside and unite behind a credible and widely accepted candidate? These are the issues. We have seen this happen all over the world. In Nigeria, those in power are winning the propaganda battle, and this is being reinforced by religious and ethnic intolerance. After 66 years of independence, an individual can come out openly to call other people “infidels” because they do not belong to his religion, and the state will not call him to order. There are many like that across the nation, operating under the cover of religion and ethnicity, with no consequences from the state. And you expect the people to rise up for justice under this condition? How many of these people have electricity to watch critics like Rufai Oseni on television? How many can afford to buy newspapers and analyse the conditions we are presently facing? So, all the big talk and social media posts will not change anything. Even if we decide to start the campaign now, it is already too late. There is no way you can defeat President Tinubu in the next election. Our opposition politicians are not serious. They are just noise-makers. The only way we can change our situation is for civil society groups to change their strategies and adopt the style of the late Gani Fawehinmi: observe critically the activities of those in government, advocate forcefully against constitutional breaches, and take them to court. We must be consistent and resilient in doing this, with vibrant unions like ASUU and other NLC affiliates. For those waiting for a miracle, you will wait in vain. Nothing will change if strong actions are not taken. Our politicians and representatives have failed us. Even in the face of strong military dictatorship, Nigerian civil society stood its ground. People like Sowore should go back to their original calling: vibrant civil rights opposition. They should forget this dream of contesting elections to become president. It will not work. The question that baffles some of us is this: Is it morally right to knowingly associate with a “crook” when it benefits you, and later turn around to point accusing fingers at him when you are on opposite sides? When you wanted Tinubu’s support, you never said he was a crook. You never shouted about his certificate. You made him your leader because you knew that through him, your party could win elections. If you knew he was a crook, why associate with him? Arguably, the only person in that setup who has not been an ally of Tinubu all this while is Peter Obi, whom many elites now prefer as their candidate. But in politics, the good guys don’t always win. We must let this lesson sink in. So, what is to be done? We must embark on massive sensitisation of the people through vibrant NGOs, civil rights groups, students, ethnic unions, religious organisations and others. Everyone must stand as a monitor of government and political activities and apply the necessary pressure to curtail excesses. No government can withstand massive people’s protests if they are carried out with sincere resolve. As for our opposition politicians, forget about them. They are not ready. •Ikhioya writes from Lagos. The post 2027: Let us end this presidential campaign charade appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nutrition: Shettima raises alarm as 41% of Nigerian children stunted
items.description: … Only 6% of pregnant women complete iron supplementation By Chioma Obinna Vice President Kashim Shettima on Tuesday in Lagos raised the alarm over Nigeria’s nutrition crisis, saying it poses a serious threat to the country’s human capital, as latest data show that 41.1 per cent of children under five are stunted, with the figure rising to 58.2 per cent in the North-West. Shettima, who spoke through his Senior Special Assistant on Public Health and Focal Person on Nutrition, Mrs Uju Rochas-Anwukah, also disclosed that only six per cent of pregnant women completed at least 180 days of iron-containing supplementation in 2024, against a national target of 70 per cent by 2035. The Vice President spoke at the opening of the 56th Annual Scientific Conference and Annual General Meeting of the Nutrition Society of Nigeria, NSN, in Lagos, themed: “Delivering Better Nutrition for All: Connecting the Dots Across Life Cycle, Systems and Sectors.” where experts called for an urgent, coordinated national response to malnutrition. Shettima said the statistics underscored the need for government, the private sector, researchers and communities to work together to reverse the country’s nutrition crisis. “Every nation writes its future twice: first in the body of the child, and later in the institutions that the child will inherit,” she said, representing Shettima. “Before intelligence becomes achievement, before labour becomes productivity, nutrition has already made its first claim on human possibility.” He said minimum dietary diversity among women of reproductive age stood at only 30 per cent, against the national target of 60 per cent by 2035. “That distance should trouble every institution represented here,” she warned. According to him, Nigeria’s nutrition policies must be judged not by the number of documents produced, but by their impact on households and communities. He said the National Nutrition Dashboard should serve as an accountability instrument for evidence-led governance, while food fortification must be assessed by its impact on micronutrient deficiencies rather than the number of regulations issued. Shettima said the Federal Government was pursuing a multisectoral approach through the National Policy on Food and Nutrition 2026–2035 and the Nutrition 774 Initiative, which seeks to take nutrition interventions to all 774 local government areas. He urged nutrition researchers and professionals to identify implementation failures early and produce evidence capable of influencing government budgets and programmes. “Good intentions do not feed a child. Budgets must be released on time, expenditures tracked, and every naira judged by measurable community impact,” he said. Speaking, the Chairman, Board of Trustees of the Nutrition Society of Nigeria, His Highness Muhammadu Sanusi II, said the latest nutrition figures should compel government to treat nutrition as a central development issue. Sanusi said 19.2 per cent of Nigerian children under five are severely stunted, stressing that nutrition was directly linked to productivity, cognitive development, maternal survival and national resilience. “Nutrition must therefore be treated as a central pillar of Nigeria’s development agenda, not a peripheral programme reserved for moments of crisis,” he said. He called for increased and protected nutrition financing, dedicated budget lines, timely releases, expenditure tracking and stronger food fortification compliance. Sanusi also urged the accelerated passage of the Nutritionists Registration Council of Nigeria Bill, saying effective regulation would strengthen professional standards and protect the public. In his welcome address, President of NSN, Professor Salisu Maiwada Abubakar, described Nigeria’s nutrition profile as “both a warning and a call to action.” Abubakar said the country must connect nutrition interventions across the life cycle, linking food systems with health, education, social protection, water and sanitation. He said the challenge was no longer simply to reduce malnutrition but to transform the systems that produce it, so that Nigerians could access safe, affordable, diverse and nutritious diets. Declaring the conference open, Permanent Secretary, Lagos State Ministry of Health, Dr Dayo Lajide, said nutrition remained critical to health, human capital development and economic growth. Lajide said Nigeria was increasingly confronted with the “triple burden” of malnutrition, comprising undernutrition, micronutrient deficiencies, overweight, obesity and diet-related non-communicable diseases. He called for stronger evidence-based policies, improved nutrition data, strengthened surveillance systems and innovative interventions targeting vulnerable groups, including women, children, adolescents and economically disadvantaged communities. Also, Director-General of NAFDAC, Professor Mojisola Adeyeye, called for stronger collaboration among regulators, nutrition professionals, academia, industry and policymakers to ensure that Nigerians have access to safe, nutritious and properly labelled foods. The conference brought together policymakers, researchers, development partners, civil society organisations and nutrition professionals to examine strategies for reversing Nigeria’s malnutrition burden. The post Nutrition: Shettima raises alarm as 41% of Nigerian children stunted appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: La pièce "El Harraz" revisitée par Amine Nassour, le 25 septembre à Rabat
items.description: La pièce de théâtre « El Harraz », l'un des chefs-d'œuvre du patrimoine théâtral marocain, revient sur les planches sous la direction du metteur en scène et dramaturge Amine Nassour, le 25 septembre au Théâtre national Mohammed V de Rabat. Mise en scène à l'origine par Tayeb Saddiki et écrite par Abdeslam Chraïbi, la pièce est présentée dans le cadre du projet de la 35è promotion de l'Institut Supérieur d'Art Dramatique et d'Animation Culturelle (ISADAC). Cette version revisitée s'inscrit dans le cadre d'une réflexion sur la mémoire théâtrale marocaine et de la réhabilitation de l'un de ses textes de référence à travers une nouvelle vision scénique. Les créateurs de cette pièce de théâtre partent de l'expérience de Tayeb Saddiki et d'Abdeslam Chraïbi, non pas comme un patrimoine à restituer tel quel, mais comme un terrain théâtral ouvert à une lecture contemporaine qui cherche à établir un dialogue entre la mémoire du spectacle marocain et la sensibilité d'une nouvelle génération d'acteurs. La représentation d' »El Harraz » sur la scène du Théâtre national Mohammed V est l'occasion de faire découvrir à une nouvelle génération de diplômés de l'ISADAC l'une des œuvres emblématiques de l'histoire du théâtre marocain, dans le cadre d'une expérience alliant formation, pratique professionnelle et réappropriation de la mémoire théâtrale dans un esprit contemporain. Créée dans les années 1960, cette pièce musicale s’inspire du patrimoine oral marocain et du répertoire du Malhoun, plus précisément du poème « El Harraz » de Cheikh El Mekki Ben El-Qorchi. The post La pièce "El Harraz" revisitée par Amine Nassour, le 25 septembre à Rabat appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Prove I left debt, I’ll stop campaigning, Obi tells Anambra govt
items.description: The Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, presidential candidate, Peter Obi, has challenged the Anambra State government to prove that his administration left behind unpaid debts, salaries, pensions or contractor liabilities. Obi issued the challenge in a statement posted on his official social media page on Monday while responding to claims by the Anambra State Government that his administration left inherited debts, including a N2 billion ecological loan. He dismissed the claims as false, saying his administration cleared historical gratuities and arrears worth more than N35 billion. Obi said there were no outstanding salaries, gratuities or pensions when he handed over to the state, adding that contractors had also been paid for projects that were duly executed and certified. On the ecological fund, Obi said the N2 billion was released about three months before the end of his tenure for the Oko/Umuchiana erosion crisis. He said he refused to spend the money and left it for his successor because it was tied to a specific project. According to Obi, the fund was separate from more than N75 billion in savings he claimed his administration left behind. “If anybody can establish anything to the contrary, I will stop campaigning,” Obi said. items.title: Labé : le trafic reprend sur l’axe Labé-Koundara après l’implication du syndicat des transporteurs
items.description: Après quelques jours d’interruption, la circulation a repris sur l’axe Labé-Koundara. Cette reprise intervient après l’implication des responsables du syndicat des transporteurs et de la mécanique générale CNTG de Labé, qui se sont rendus sur le terrain pour rencontrer les autorités et échanger sur les difficultés rencontrées par les chauffeurs. Selon Maître Tanou Nadhél Diallo, secrétaire général du syndicat des transporteurs et de la mécanique générale CNTG de Labé, cette démarche a permis de mieux comprendre la situation sur cet axe stratégique. « Nous sommes allés à la rencontre des autorités. Le premier constat est que le nombre des barrages routiers sur l’axe Labé-Koundara est revu à la hausse. Sur place, nous avons été reçus par les autorités et, au cours des échanges, elles nous ont rappelé que les chauffeurs doivent être dans les normes pour pouvoir circuler, c’est-à-dire disposer du permis de conduire, de la carte grise du véhicule, des papiers d’assurance du véhicule, du triangle rouge, entre autres », indique-t-il. Pour le responsable syndical, le respect des documents administratifs et des règles de circulation constitue une condition essentielle pour permettre aux transporteurs d’exercer leur activité dans de bonnes conditions. Il invite ainsi les chauffeurs à se mettre en règle, notamment en ce qui concerne le permis de conduire. « Nous demandons aux chauffeurs d’être dans les normes et d’être en possession des documents, notamment le permis de conduire, car on ne peut pas être conducteur d’un véhicule de transport sans avoir un permis », souligne-t-il. Maître Tanou Nadhél Diallo appelle également les transporteurs à changer leur perception des agents des services de sécurité présents sur les différents points de contrôle. « Les chauffeurs doivent cesser de croire que les services de sécurité sont nos ennemis. Ce sont nos partenaires. Il est donc important d’adopter un comportement responsable devant les agents de sécurité », ajoute-t-il. La reprise du trafic sur l’axe Labé-Koundara devrait permettre aux voyageurs et aux opérateurs économiques de retrouver progressivement leurs habitudes de déplacement et de transport des marchandises. Le syndicat appelle toutefois les chauffeurs au respect des règles en vigueur et à une collaboration responsable avec les services de sécurité afin de favoriser une circulation plus apaisée sur cet axe. Alpha Moussa Dieng, correspondant régional à Labé L’article Labé : le trafic reprend sur l’axe Labé-Koundara après l’implication du syndicat des transporteurs est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: RD Congo: 3e mandat sur orbite, opposants piégés!
items.description: Un «guet-apens»! Sans détour, c’est ainsi que l’opposition a qualifié la fin prématurée de sa manifestation de ce mardi 15 septembre 2026. Une marche qu’elle a voulu hautement politique, la faisant coïncider avec la rentrée des députés qui avait pour plat du jour, la session budgétaire. Et c’est pour réaffirmer aux élus du peuple leur ferme volonté de faire échec au 3e mandat sous le charme duquel Felix Tshisekedi est, visiblement, tombé, que les opposants avaient décidé de battre le pavé, et de se rassembler non loin du Palais du peuple, siège des parlementaires. Mais, la marche a pris fin en queue de poisson, dispersée en face du QG de l’Union pour la démocratie et le progrès (UDPS), le parti au pouvoir. A qui la faute? Aux Forces de progrès, «la milice privée du pouvoir», accusent des opposants désabusés, dont la manifestation avait pourtant reçu l’autorisation officielle requise! Un «guet-apens» en plein Kinshasa! Pas dans le Kivu où les combattants de l’AFC/M23, règnent en maîtres et tiennent en joue, des populations malmenées par l’épidémie dévastarice de l’Ebola, dans sa nouvelle souche, l’espèce Bundibugyo! Et si c’était depuis le début, c’est-à-dire à la vue de l’itinéraire de la marche que le «guet-apens» a été concocté avec minutie, faisant du passage devant le siège de l’UDPS à Kinshasa, l’endroit propice pour organiser la débandade des opposants qui osent aller contre le désir du prince? Rien, surtout pas des opposants aux mains nues, ne doit contrarier le plan de Felix Tshisikedi, si proche de son but. La loi sur le référendum constitutionnelle est déjà dans les tiroirs et tout est mis en œuvre par le pouvoir et ses partisans pour que la représentation théâtrale aille à son terme. Le texte, avec la caution des parlementaires, passera devant le peuple et ce dernier, qu’il dise «oui» ou «non», verra les urnes vomir des chiffres staliniens en faveur du «oui». Ainsi se passent presque toutes, pour ne pas dire toutes les élections en Afrique, surtout quand il s’agit d’assurer le pouvoir du chef. Que pourra donc une opposition qui va constamment tomber dans le «guet-apens» d’un pouvoir aux mains d’un ancien opposant bercé depuis son enfance par la voix d’un père, feu Etienne Tshisekedi, qui a porté, jusqu’au seuil de sa mort, la contestation contre les pouvoirs sans partage de Mobutu Sese Seko et des père et fils Kabila? Non seulement Felix Tshisekedi a la force aveugle du pouvoir, mais il maîtrise l’art machiavélique du diviser pour régner, un autre «guet-apens» qui avale rapidement certains opposants avides de la courte échelle, trop vite séduits par les espèces sonnantes et trébuchantes et les strapontins politiques. Dire que c’est dans cette ambiance délétère, envers et contre tous, bien entendu hormis ses zélateurs, que Felix Tshisekedi entend organiser un dialogue qu’il dit inclusif, mais dont il éloigne les principaux protagonistes que sont les vrais opposants et les leaders de guerre. En réalité, c’est bien un monologue exclusif que vise Felix Tshisekedi pour faire prospérer le leurre de la paix et donner toutes les chances à son entreprise de changement de la constitution qui lui ouvrira le boulevard de la présidence à vie, avec pour première étape décisive, le 3e mandat. Ainsi va la RD Congo de Felix Tshisekedi! Par Wakat Séra L’article RD Congo: 3e mandat sur orbite, opposants piégés! est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: A closer look at the Zero Rated Access Initiative, by Okoh Aihe
items.description: The NCC programme wasn’t part of my schedule last week but the insistence of a young employee drew me to the Hilton, venue of the programme, and I left very appreciative that I found my way there. Sometimes, you need to clear your schedule to do certain things. This was one of them. As I write now, I am still checking my body to see whether there are some tiny pieces of confetti that rained down at the launch of the Zero Rated Access Initiative by the Commission’s Board. I was only too happy to see history unfold and, all the while, contemplating how this will affect the education sector and the future of the young ones who will inherit this nation. Yet, this is a project creatively minted by the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) and the telecommunications operators that reached out to the Ministry of Education with life-transforming news of giving out free data to enable young Nigerians to access some education platforms free of charge. I have always written in this column that a good working relationship between top government functionaries, between ministries and their parastatals, between chief executives and their counterparts, and even between the National Assembly and agencies and industries, will generate something great for the nation. Last week, there was a demonstration of that, and what seems like a well-nurtured traction between NCC, under the Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, and the Ministry of Education, has led to something great that will positively transform young lives well beyond our time. The idea behind the Zero Rated Access Initiative, according to the NCC Board, is to promote digital inclusion and enhance access to educational resources for students; thus prompting a valuable collaboration of the Federal Ministry of Education and other stakeholders, including the telecom operators, whose role provides the real oxygen for the entire process. One of its members, Rimini H. Makama, Executive Commissioner Stakeholder Management (ECSM), said at the launch on September 10, that the initiative is built to give every Nigerian learner a fair chance at digital education, pointing out that learning has moved online, prompting students to rely on online courses and digital libraries, among others, which all depend on connectivity that may be a scarce resource to some learners. In her words: “The Zero-Rated Access Initiative exists to erase that line. Its principle is simple: no learner should be shut out of educational content because of where they live or what their family earns. By providing data allowances for approved educational platforms, it turns potential into opportunity, so that more young Nigerians can learn, research, build and acquire the skills a digital economy demands.” Dr Tunji Alausa, the Education Minister, who could hardly contain himself, declared excitedly, “Today’s launch represents much more than a telecommunications initiative. It is an education intervention. And most importantly, it is an investment in the future of millions of young Nigerians.” He appealed for us to build a Nigeria where geography does not determine educational opportunity, where poverty does not prevent a child from accessing knowledge, but a country with an education system where technology becomes a great equaliser—opening doors, expanding possibilities and empowering every learner to realise his or her full potential. In simple terms, the Zero-Rated Access Initiative (ZRAI) is designed to give a data allowance of 100MB to 5 million learners or students at N100 per day. This comes to N15bn a month and totals a whopping N180bn a year for 5 million students. This amount can give a learning average of between 2 and 5 hours daily on education websites—Reading texts/PDFs and Google searches: 5–15 MB/hour (7–20 hours); online learning platforms (mostly text): 10–25 MB/hour (4–10 hours). For some of us who could only afford education because the late Chief Obafemi Awolowo offered free education through his party, UPN, and could hardly encounter a telephone until well into the university, the launch last Thursday meant so much. It was almost very emotional as it destroyed status, class, and privileges. I have seen so many young people condemn the initiative, saying 100MB is hardly a drop in the ocean. I think this needs an explanation. The Zero Rated Access Initiative is a major corporate social responsibility (CSR) package put together by the regulator and the telecom operators for Nigerian students because of a shared concern for those who suffer digital exclusion. The NCC Board said the Initiative will go live on October 1, 2026, and reaffirmed its commitment to monitoring its sustainable implementation. Meanwhile, the Education Minister informed that the initiative will commence with learners at the senior secondary school level and tertiary institutions and subsequently expand to other categories of learners across the country. Some operators—Karl Toriola, CEO of MTN, Dinesh Balsingh of Airtel, and Obafemi Banigbe of T2 Mobile—addressed the launch virtually and promised continuing support and sustainability of the initiative. However, it was the industry representative at the event, Engr. Gbenga Adebayo, who is the chairman of the Association of Licensed Telecom Operators of Nigeria (ALTON), who further articulated the position of his members to this writer, shortly after the launch. “For a student,” he explained, “100MB can provide meaningful daily access to learning materials, examination preparation, research and educational platforms without worrying about the cost of data. The programme currently provides 100 MB of daily access to approved platforms, including the Ministry of Education platforms and WAEC learning resources.” Adebayo is excited about the tripartite initiative, which, he said, “is essentially a partnership around a common national objective. The Ministry identifies and provides the educational content and platforms; NCC provides the regulatory coordination and oversight; and the operators provide the network infrastructure and connectivity that allow students and educators to access the content. So, it is a good example of government and industry working together to achieve digital inclusion and improve education.” He canvassed the position of ALTON members not to allow the initiative to flag or fail, saying, “They have willingly supported the programme because we believe that investing in education is investing in Nigeria’s future. But zero-rating has a real cost to the operators—it consumes network resources and creates an open-ended financial and operational obligation if participation and usage are not properly managed.” Adebayo argued that “sustainability of the initiative should not necessarily mean that the operators want a commercial return from the students. What we need is a fair, predictable and sustainable framework—including proper beneficiary registration or opt-in, user controls, monitoring of usage and mechanisms to prevent abuse. This ensures that the benefits reach genuine students and learners while allowing operators to continue investing in the networks on which the programme depends.” “In short, the operators are saying: we are willing to support the national education agenda, but the programme must be designed in a way that can survive and be sustained. The objective is not to withdraw the benefit; it is to make sure we can keep providing it for the long term,” as he painted a picture of hope. In the week following the furore generated by New York City’s new guidelines and restrictions, limiting student screen time and technology use in public schools, including the use of AI, starting from September 2026, a move being watched by the rest of the United States, it was interesting to see whether such fears would haunt the introduction of the Zero Rated Access Initiative. The Education Minister seems to have addressed such fears when he declared that Zero-rating should not mean indiscriminate access to every platform that describes itself as educational. The content made available to our children must be appropriate, credible, safe, and aligned with our educational objectives and curriculum, Alausa said. However, beautiful as the initiative may look, I have my fears that it will exacerbate the digital divide immediately. Digital connectivity is poor in most rural parts of the country I have been to, and although the Board informed that infrastructure commitments by the operators are being met—8,526 out of 12,179 sites built recently to expand network coverage, capacity and quality of experience (QoE)—I am constrained to wonder whether vandalism of telecommunications infrastructure is not happening at a faster pace. Apart from the pervasive insecurity, telecom service delivery is sabotaged, even by state agencies. This will demand further rigorous planning by the regulator to build more alliances that can strengthen the industry and position operators to meet fresh demands from the state for its citizens. The Zero-Rated Access Initiative is a good one, but the guardrails need to be strong enough to lead to a future that looks very promising. items.title: Chinese defense minister urges deeper cooperation on global security
items.description: The Chinese military is willing to work with all parties to deepen practical cooperation, jointly address global security challenges, and resolutely safeguard world and regional peace and stability, Minister of National Defense Dong Jun said on Tuesday. Dong made the remarks during separate meetings in Beijing with defense officials from Myanmar, Brunei, Belarus, Azerbaijan, Kyrgyzstan and Armenia, as well as ASEAN Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn, who are in Beijing to attend the 13th Beijing Xiangshan Forum, which is scheduled to run from Tuesday to Thursday. Dong welcomed the guests to the Beijing Xiangshan Forum, saying that over the past 20 years, the forum has upheld the principles of equality, openness, inclusiveness and mutual learning, contributing wisdom to promoting peace and cooperation and advancing common security. He said that amid growing instability and uncertainty in the international landscape, the Chinese military is ready to work with all parties to implement the vision of a community with a shared future for humanity and the four major global initiatives. Themed "Build Consensus on Stability, Advance Security Governance Together," this year's forum has drawn attendees from almost 100 countries, regions and international organizations. Over the past two decades, the forum has evolved into a vital international public good, offering a space for equal dialogue and joint efforts toward global peace.

items.title: China to work with ASEAN for closer community with shared future
items.description: China is willing to work with ASEAN to build a closer China-ASEAN community with a shared future, Foreign Minister Wang Yi said when meeting with Secretary-General of ASEAN Kao Kim Hourn on Tuesday. Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said China attaches great importance to ASEAN and regards it as a priority in its neighborhood diplomacy. Noting that this year marks the fifth anniversary of the establishment of the China-ASEAN comprehensive strategic partnership and the 35th anniversary of China-ASEAN dialogue relations, Wang said both sides face new opportunities for the development of relations. China will continue to support ASEAN's unity and its centrality in the regional architecture, he said. Wang noted that maintaining peace and stability in the South China Sea is in line with the common interests of countries in the region. He added that China is willing to work with ASEAN countries to implement the Declaration on the Conduct of Parties in the South China Sea (DOC), move forward consultations on a code of conduct in the South China Sea, and jointly foster a new narrative of peace, stability, cooperation and friendship. For his part, Kao said ASEAN is willing to share opportunities and meet challenges with China, continue to deepen and expand practical cooperation in various fields, and promote ASEAN-China relations to constantly reach new heights. ASEAN is ready to work with China to jointly maintain peace and stability in the South China Sea, he added.

items.title: Modernisation du service public : Le Premier ministre lance FasoSign pour concrétiser le « zéro papier »
items.description: Le Camarade Premier ministre, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, a présidé ce mardi 15 septembre 2026 à Ouagadougou le lancement officiel de FasoSign, la plateforme nationale de signature électronique. S'inscrivant dans la dynamique du « zéro papier » à l'horizon 2030, cet outil souverain vise à éliminer l'impression et les déplacements physiques, à réduire les délais de traitement et à moderniser en profondeur l'Administration au service des citoyens. Le mardi 15 septembre 2026 marque une étape majeure dans la modernisation des services publics au Burkina Faso. Présidé par le Premier ministre, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, le lancement officiel de la plateforme nationale FasoSign apporte le maillon qui manquait à la dématérialisation complète des démarches administratives. Jusqu'ici, bien que plusieurs dizaines de services publics et plus d'une centaine de plateformes soient déjà opérationnels en ligne, la signature manuscrite constituait un frein persistant. Elle imposait l'impression papier, l'acheminement physique et des déplacements répétés pour valider des actes essentiels tels que les ordres de mission générés sur les plateformes CIM et CIM-EXT. Désormais, grâce à FasoSign, l'ensemble du processus — de la production à la conservation, en passant par la validation et la signature — peut s'effectuer intégralement en ligne. Inscrite dans le cadre de la modernisation de l'Administration engagée sous les orientations du Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, cette infrastructure s'accompagne d'une exigence ferme de résultats. Lors de son intervention, le Chef du Gouvernement a martelé que FasoSign ne doit pas être perçue comme une simple option, mais comme une obligation pour assurer le fonctionnement d'une Administration moderne, performante et rapide. « L’Administration doit être au service du citoyen, du peuple révolutionnaire », a-t-il rappelé, en exigeant la réduction des délais d'attente. Pour transformer cette avancée technique en réussite concrète, le Premier ministre a engagé le ministère de la Transition digitale ainsi que l'ensemble des départements ministériels et institutions publiques à établir sans délai un chronogramme rigoureux de vulgarisation et d'adoption. Présentée par la ministre de la Transition digitale, des Postes et des Communications électroniques, Dr Aminata Zerbo née Sabané, FasoSign se dresse comme une infrastructure nationale et un service de confiance central. Sur le plan technique et juridique, la plateforme apporte des garanties éprouvées en matière d'authenticité, d'intégrité et de traçabilité des documents. Sur le plan financier et logistique, elle permet de réduire drastiquement les coûts liés à l'impression, au transport et à l'archivage physique. Surtout, l'outil revêt une portée stratégique fondamentale : les clés, certificats et actes signés relèvent directement de la souveraineté numérique de l'État burkinabè. Le déploiement de FasoSign s’insère directement dans les douze chantiers de la transformation digitale à l’horizon 2030, qui portent notamment les ambitions nationales du « zéro papier » et du « zéro cash » dans les services publics. En venant compléter l'écosystème numérique existant, la plateforme permet de produire, valider, signer, transmettre et conserver les actes sous forme dématérialisée. Cette avancée décisive ouvre la voie à une bureaucratie plus fluide, plus accessible et pleinement réactive face aux besoins des usagers. items.title: I am off the streets – Singer Tems
items.description: Nigerian singer Temilade Openiyi, popularly known as Tems, has announced that she has “left the streets”, a term commonly used for women who are getting married or are no longer searching for love. The Grammy-winning singer disclosed this during a TikTok livestream on Monday but did not elaborate. She, however, explained that she was leaving the streets because she was tired of men wasting her time. “I don’t like it when guys waste my time. But for me, never again. I don’t have that problem anymore. I have left the streets; I wouldn’t even say I was ever on the streets,” she said. Tems has previously lamented how most of the men who approach her always have ulterior motives. In an interview with YouTuber Korty EO last year, Tems revealed that many of the men who approached her for relationships were mostly interested in her body. She said she would have preferred genuine and deeper connections.

items.title: Bobo-Dioulasso : Un célibataire de 43 ans risque 2 ans de prison pour avoir eu des rapports sexuels par voie anale avec une mineure de 13ans
items.description: Toni (nom d’emprunt) âgé de 43 ans, célibataire et sans enfant, a comparu ce lundi 14 septembre 2026 devant le Tribunal de grande instance de Bobo-Dioulasso, siégeant en matière criminelle. Il est poursuivi pour des faits qualifiés de viol aggravé sur une mineure âgée de 13 ans et 11 mois. Les faits Selon les éléments factuels présentés à l’audience, Toni est accusé d’avoir imposé à Bali (nom d’emprunt), une mineure âgée de 13 ans, un rapport sexuel par voie anale, sous la menace d’une arme blanche. D’après la mère de la victime, Bali avait quitté temporairement le domicile familial pour séjourner chez sa grand-mère. À son retour, sa mère aurait constaté qu’elle éprouvait des difficultés à s’asseoir normalement et à aller convenablement à la selle. Interrogée à plusieurs reprises, la jeune fille aurait finalement révélé avoir été victime d’un viol et désigné Toni comme l’auteur des faits. Toni ne reconnaît pas les faits À la barre, Toni a catégoriquement nié avoir commis un viol. Il a toutefois reconnu avoir eu des rapports sexuels avec la mineure, soutenant que ceux-ci auraient été consentis. Selon ses déclarations, Bali serait venue une première fois chez lui et ils se seraient entendus sur une somme de 2 500 F CFA. Elle serait revenue une seconde fois, dans les mêmes conditions. Des explications que la victime a fermement contestées. Interrogée sur les déclarations de l’accusé, elle a affirmé qu’elle n’avait consenti à aucun des rapports sexuels. « Pourquoi tu n’as pas crié ? » Au cours des échanges avec le tribunal, une question a particulièrement retenu l’attention : « Pourquoi tu n’as pas crié ? » La mineure a expliqué qu’elle n’avait pas crié parce que Toni aurait tenu un couteau au moment des faits. Une version que l’accusé a contestée, niant avoir utilisé un couteau pour la menacer. Le tribunal a également cherché à savoir si la victime avait reçu de l’argent après les faits. — As-tu reçu de l’argent après l’acte ? — « Oui, il m’a remis un chewing-gum et 500 F CFA », a-t-elle répondu. L’accusé demande pardon Invité à prendre la parole, Toni s’est principalement contenté de demander pardon. Le ministère public a alors souhaité savoir pourquoi il sollicitait le pardon du tribunal alors qu’il continuait à contester le caractère forcé des rapports. L’accusé a expliqué qu’il demandait pardon parce qu’il ne se portait pas bien. À la suite des déclarations de la victime, le tribunal a procédé à la lecture de certains éléments du dossier avant de lui demander si elle maintenait ses déclarations. Bali a répondu par l’affirmative. Des précisions sur le lieu et l’heure des faits Pour mieux cerner les circonstances des faits, le tribunal a également interrogé la victime sur le moment et le cadre dans lequel ils se seraient déroulés. Bali a indiqué que les faits auraient eu lieu aux environs de 19 heures, dans la maison où résidait Toni. Elle a décrit une habitation où l’accusé dormait sur une natte. Elle a également précisé que des personnes se trouvaient dans la cour ce jour-là et révisaient, mais qu’aucune d’entre elles n’aurait eu connaissance de ce qui se passait. La mère ne réclame aucune réparation Le tribunal s’est ensuite intéressé aux éventuelles réclamations de la famille de la victime, dans l’hypothèse où l’accusé serait déclaré coupable. La mère de Bali a indiqué qu’elle ne réclamait rien. Le tribunal a alors voulu savoir ce qu’il en était du père de la jeune fille. — Et le père de l’enfant ? « Nous ne sommes plus ensemble », a répondu la mère. — Mais concernant cette affaire, il n’a rien dit ? « Oui, je lui fais des comptes rendus. Mais il ne m’a pas dit non plus de réclamer quelque chose », a-t-elle expliqué. Le parquet requiert deux ans de prison ferme Dans ses réquisitions, le ministère public a rappelé que les faits remontent au mois de mars 2026. Selon le parquet, Toni aurait imposé à la mineure un rapport sexuel par voie anale et l’aurait menacée avec un couteau. Le procureur a également relevé une contradiction dans la défense de l’accusé : selon le ministère public, Toni ne nie pas l’existence des rapports sexuels, mais soutient qu’ils auraient été consentis. Le parquet a par ailleurs insisté sur les conséquences que de tels faits pourraient avoir sur la santé mentale et psychologique de la victime. Le procureur a notamment lancé un appel à la prise en compte des conséquences potentielles de ces actes sur la jeune fille. Au terme de ses réquisitions, le ministère public a demandé au tribunal de maintenir Toni dans les liens de la prévention, de le déclarer coupable et de le condamner à deux ans d’emprisonnement ferme ainsi qu’à une amende de 500 000 F CFA assortie du sursis. Le tribunal a pris acte des réquisitions et a mis l’affaire en délibéré. Le verdict est attendu le 12 octobre 2026. items.title: Gombe vows to end open defecation
items.description: By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Gombe State Government has reiterated its determination to improve the water, sanitation and hygiene, WASH, sector and achieve an open-defecation-free state. The commitment was reaffirmed as the Gombe State Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Agency, RUWASSA, under the Sustainable Urban and Rural Water Supply, Sanitation and Hygiene, SURWASH, programme, intensified sensitisation and mobilisation campaigns across Local Government Areas that have claimed Open Defecation Free, ODF, status. The campaign commenced with a mega rally in Nafada Local Government Area, where RUWASSA engaged traditional rulers, community leaders, government officials and other stakeholders to strengthen community ownership of sanitation initiatives and sustain hygiene practices ahead of the ODF validation exercise. The RUWASSA delegation, led by its General Manager, Engr. Mohammed Ahmed Gibrimu, FNSE, FNICE, who was represented by the Sector Lead, WASH, Yahaya Umaru, began the mobilisation at the Nafada Local Government Secretariat before proceeding to the palace of the Emir of Nafada. Speaking at the palace, Umaru, who conveyed the General Manager’s message, commended the Emir of Nafada, HRH Alhaji Muhammadu Dadum Hamza, as well as residents and stakeholders in the LGA for their collective efforts towards improving sanitation and hygiene. He said RUWASSA, in collaboration with the local government and other stakeholders, had continued to provide technical and institutional support towards achieving and sustaining ODF status in the area. According to him, following Nafada LGA’s declaration of ODF status, RUWASSA had submitted the required documentation to the National Task Group on Sanitation, NTGS, for review ahead of the anticipated validation exercise. He urged residents to sustain the momentum by maintaining proper sanitation and hygiene practices before, during and after the validation exercise. Also speaking, the Sanitation Specialist, Alhaji Hussaini Abdulkadir, commended the people and stakeholders of Nafada for the progress recorded, stressing the need for sustained public awareness and, where necessary, effective enforcement of sanitation laws. Earlier, in a welcome address, the Chairman of Nafada LGA, Hon. Babangida Adamu Jigawa, represented by his Deputy, Hon. Gambo Yahaya, commended Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya for his continued support for the WASH sector. He also appreciated RUWASSA for its technical support, assuring that the local government was prepared and committed to a successful ODF validation exercise. Responding, the Emir of Nafada, HRH Alhaji Muhammadu Dadum Hamza, welcomed the RUWASSA delegation and commended the agency for prioritising Nafada in its sanitation and hygiene interventions. The traditional ruler noted that while attaining ODF status was a significant milestone, the ultimate objective remained the protection of the health and wellbeing of residents. He urged the people of the emirate to support and sustain the sanitation campaign, disclosing that sanctions had already been introduced against persons who violate sanitation laws. According to him, offenders would face a fine of N10,000, in addition to community service or heavy labour. As part of the mobilisation exercise, the Emir directed the eight district heads in the area to appear before the gathering and provide updates on the preparedness of their respective communities for the ODF validation. Reports and testimonies presented by traditional and community leaders indicated a high level of preparedness across the LGA and reinforced the area’s readiness for the anticipated validation exercise. The mega rally attracted government officials, WASH stakeholders, traditional and community leaders, civil society organisations, security agencies and members of the media. The participation of the Makadan Sarki also added traditional colour to the mobilisation, which formed part of RUWASSA’s broader efforts to strengthen sanitation and hygiene practices, consolidate ODF achievements and contribute to the realisation of a cleaner, healthier and open-defecation-free Gombe State.
