items.title: A Shouting Match and an Ultimatum at the Kennedy Center
items.description: Donald Trump has given the federal judiciary an ultimatum: Let him put his name on the Kennedy Center, or he won’t save it. That threat came after a federal judge, Christopher Cooper, today blocked yet another effort to add the president’s name to the building. Moments later, Trump virtually joined a Kennedy Center board meeting, at which he slammed Cooper’s decision and lashed out at Representative Joyce Beatty—the ex officio board member challenging his overhaul of the institution in court—according to a person with knowledge of the meeting, who spoke with me on the condition of anonymity to discuss internal proceedings. Later, Trump posted on Truth Social that the center’s “Renovation and Reconstruction, which is a very large and complex job, cannot begin until such time as the D.C. Circuit rules on the Board’s approved name,” adding, “If the ruling is a negative one, which it should not be, and is not overturned by the U.S. Supreme Court, the Reconstruction and the Renovation of The Kennedy Center will not take place.” After months defined by empty theaters and canceled shows, the Kennedy Center has become a shadow of the premier performance venue it was just over a year ago. A Washington Post report this week revealed that the center’s finances are on the brink of collapse and that it could face bankruptcy. But while the institution has diminished, its leaders—and Trump’s allies on the board—have continued to push his plans forward, repackaging their oft-repeated claim that the only way to save it from financial ruin ahead of a two-year renovation is to emblazon it with Trump’s name. The crisis at the Kennedy Center is entangled in a larger effort by Trump to control what Washington looks like—a fight that has taken on higher stakes as his administration evades federal procedures designed to protect historic places from the whims of any one president. The immediate outcome of today’s events adds more confusion. General trustees voted in favor of closing the center, and two staffers told me that leaders subsequently announced through the building’s broadcast system that the Kennedy Center was closed to the public. It was unclear if that announcement meant that employees would also be barred from the premises, according to one of the staffers, both of whom spoke with me on the condition of anonymity for fear of reprisal. Cooper issued a preliminary injunction in May to temporarily block the center from closing; if he does not lift or amend that ruling, the announced closure will put the board in violation of the court’s orders. [ Read: Trump’s Kennedy Center shakedown ] “The Board’s decision today reflects sound judgment and a clear prioritization of safety above all else,” the center’s vice president for public relations, Roma Daravi, told me in a statement. “As the main building closes for urgent renovations—long overdue and desperately needed to protect the safety of patrons, artists and staff—the Center remains committed to pursuing a safe and efficient renovation through all legal means.” The White House referred me to Trump’s post when I asked for comment on this story. Meanwhile, the latest evidence of trouble at the Kennedy Center is scattered on the velvet carpet in the Grand Foyer, after a portion of its ceiling collapsed during a storm on September 4. The incident, which did not result in any injuries, has become the primary example for leaders describing the building’s urgent needs—and, as Daravi put it, debate whether “decades of neglect and deferred maintenance” are to blame. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick doubled down last night, posting security footage of the moment the chunks of ceiling suddenly fell to the floor. “If a performance had been underway, patrons could have been killed,” he wrote . The rubble and the hole in the ceiling are still on full display, while signs, ropes, and a yellow cone caution people against entering the foyer. The fallen ceiling has become a key image of the Kennedy Center’s crisis. Trump’s allies say it’s proof that the building’s troubles predate this administration, and can be resolved only by the appropriately recognized intervention of the president-as-master-builder. But to some who oppose his overhaul, the center’s loud publicization of the problem underscores the board’s eagerness—perhaps overeagerness—to shut down the building. In a filing this week, Beatty’s team alleged that the center was citing the ceiling damage as justification for closure, but pointed out that a similar problem in 1977 was addressed without shutting down the center. (Beatty’s lawyers told the court that further discovery could show that mismanagement under Trump led to the institution’s insolvency.) Either way, after the board’s latest vote to close, the next step is to wait and see if Cooper will allow it this time. It’s unclear if anything he heard today will persuade him—including a lengthy assessment of the building’s conditions that a real-estate firm prepared for the board—given his previous statement that the initial closure plans were “ill-informed and seemingly preordained.” But a crumbling ceiling might just do the trick: During the hearing today, Cooper indicated that he would consider amending his preliminary injunction to authorize closure for urgent circumstances. [ Read: What I saw inside the Kennedy Center ] The other emergency—the money—is even messier. The Washington Post reported on Sunday that Kennedy Center leaders are warning trustees of financial collapse within weeks, saying that the institution could soon be unable to make payroll or cover routine bills. The alarm follows an earlier Post report on internal financial records showing that the center could face a deficit of $23 million —even amid its drastic spending cuts this year. To keep Trump’s plans for the center alive, the board has already appealed today’s ruling against adding his name to the facade, and Beatty revealed in a court filing to Cooper that leaders had been weighing 10 different ways in which Trump’s name could be added back to the center’s edifice. “The Board seeks to provide multiple options so that President Trump can be legally and appropriately recognized and acknowledged on the facade of the Kennedy Center so that he agrees to carry the burden of managing the renovation and provides the Center with a much required financial rescue,” a resolution that the board had prepared for this week read, though it was later dropped from the board’s agenda so trustees could focus exclusively on closure. In his ruling today, Cooper reiterated the conclusion he had already reached four months ago. “Simply put, Defendants cannot install memorials for President Trump or anyone or anything else at the Kennedy Center without Congress’s blessing,” he wrote, adding that the latest renaming plan “bucks a federal court order and a statute Congress enacted.” Trump’s reaction today to Cooper’s decision—both online and before the board—underscores the bargain that has defined his stewardship of the Kennedy Center. Its leaders say that it is nearing financial and structural collapse, and that Trump is uniquely capable of raising the money and overseeing the work to turn the institution around. Today’s hearing brought up new questions about those claims, including what bankruptcy would even mean for a charitable trust organization created by Congress. If its finances are truly as bad as leaders and reports say, the court might eventually need to consider placing the center under the control of an independent receiver. For now, the venue is trapped between self-inflicted crises and the conditions that have been attached to solving them. But saving the Kennedy Center may ultimately require something its leadership has gone out of its way to resist: separating the future of the institution from the wishes of the president.

items.title: Suivi de la campagne agropastorale 2026-2027 : Le ministre Ismaël Sombié salue la résilience des producteurs à Fada N’Gourma
items.description: Au cours de sa sortie de terrain dans la région du Goulmou, lundi 14 septembre 2026, le ministre d’État, ministre de l’Agriculture, des Ressources animales et halieutiques, le commandant Ismaël Sombié, a visité le centre d’exploitation agricole de la maison d’arrêt et de correction et le chantier de l’abattoir frigorifique moderne de Fada N’Gourma. Il a également lancé les travaux de construction de l’adduction d’eau potable de ladite localité. Les cultures présentent une bonne physionomie dans le Goulmou et la Tapoa et passable dans la Tapoa " data-large-file="https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/A1-1024x683.jpeg" aria-label="Ouvrez l’image en plein écran." /> Les cultures présentent une bonne physionomie dans le Goulmou et la Tapoa et passable dans la Tapoa Face aux informations alarmistes véhiculées sur les réseaux sociaux en lien avec les poches de sécheresse dans le pays, le ministre d’État, ministre de l’Agriculture, des Ressources animales et halieutiques, le commandant Ismaël Sombié, a entrepris une tournée dans les régions du Goulmou et du Nakambé pour toucher du doigt les réalités sur le terrain. Pour le premier jour de cette sortie, lundi 14 septembre 2026, le ministre Sombié a d’abord visité le centre d’exploitation agricole de la Maison d’arrêt et de correction (MAC) de Fada N’Gourma. À l’occasion, le directeur régional chargé de l’agriculture du Goulmou, Bassirou Mandé, a soutenu que la campagne agropastorale 2026-2027 s’annonce sous de bons auspices dans leur région, malgré des disparités locales. « En dépit d’un démarrage étalé entre juin et juillet, selon les provinces, le niveau de la pluviométrie globale est jugé bon, avec une moyenne de 631 mm d’eau déjà enregistrée, des chiffres équivalents à ceux de l’année précédente. Sur les 20 postes pluviométriques suivis dans la région, 10 présentent une situation excédentaire, notamment à Fada, Diabo, Matiacoali, avec des hauteurs d’eau atteignant 750 à 830 mm », a affirmé le directeur régional. En termes d’opération culturale, a-t-il ajouté, c’est le butage et le traitement phytosanitaire qui sont en cours dans la région. Sur le plan végétatif, il a confié que les cultures présentent une bonne physionomie dans le Goulmou et la Tapoa et passable dans le Sirba, car le riz est en phase d’épiaison-floraison, tandis que le maïs et le niébé atteignent la maturité. « Si la pluviométrie se maintient jusqu’en fin octobre, nous allons atteindre les prévisions céréalières de la région », a-t-il rassuré. Afin de soutenir cette dynamique, M. Mandé a précisé que des appuis étatiques consécutifs ont été déployés dans les trois régions de l’Est du pays. « Ce qui a permis d’aménager 420 hectares de bas-fonds, accompagnés de la distribution de 420 tonnes de semences et de 1 100 tonnes d’engrais subventionnés. Un parc de 26 tracteurs a permis de labourer 2 600 hectares au profit des producteurs. La SOBMAP a disponibilisé environ 400 tonnes d’engrais pour la vente à prix raisonnés », a-t-il détaillé. Des personnes réinstallées appuyées Suite aux efforts de sécurisation ayant permis le retour de populations dans leurs localités, a-t-il poursuivi, près de 1 000 ménages réinstallés ont bénéficié d’un soutien spécifique en équipements, à savoir des motoculteurs et des intrants. Les acteurs de la filière viande à s’approprier ce l’abattoir frigorifique moderne de Fada N’Gourma, qui sera bientôt à disposition. À entendre le directeur régional, bien que la campagne agricole soit jugée très bonne dans le Gourma et la Tapoa, quelques poches de sécheresse d’une superficie d’environ 100 hectares de cultures ont été relevées dans la province de la Gnagna, notamment à Bogandé, Thion et Mani. La menace concerne des spéculations comme l’arachide, le niébé et le sorgho. Faisant cas du centre d’exploitation agricole du centre pénitentiaire de Fada N’Gourma, il a indiqué que, sur un site de 10 hectares, les pensionnaires ont exploité une superficie de 8,55 hectares. Ils y ont produit du maïs (13,5 tonnes attendues), du sorgho (5,3 tonnes), du niébé (1,4 tonne) et du riz (les variétés TS2 et Orylux, avec 2,4 tonnes attendues). Selon le SG de l’ONEA, Salifou Ouédraogo, Fada N’Gouma ne devrait plus connaître de pénurie avec la mise en service de cette adduction d’eau potable, à partir d’avril 2027. " data-large-file="https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/A3-1024x683.jpeg" aria-label="Ouvrez l’image en plein écran." /> Selon le SG de l’ONEA, Salifou Ouédraogo, Fada N’Gouma ne devrait plus connaître de pénurie avec la mise en service de cette adduction d’eau potable, à partir d’avril 2027. Le centre abrite également deux poulaillers d’une capacité totale de 2 500 têtes. Accompagnée par les services techniques de l’agriculture, cette initiative génère une marge brute estimée à plus de 3,3 millions de F CFA. « Une partie des récoltes vient constituer des stocks de sécurité directement affectés à l’alimentation des détenus, réduisant la charge de l’État tout en offrant une formation qualifiante aux pensionnaires », s’est-il réjoui. Le ministre Sombié a soutenu que l’exploitation agricole de la MAC de Fada illustre la vision gouvernementale d’autonomisation des centres pénitentiaires. Saluant la résilience des producteurs de Fada et le travail accompli sur ledit site, Ismaël Sombié a rappelé que cette approche s’inscrit dans la refondation du système judiciaire et carcéral, à travers >. Il s’agit, selon lui, de transformer les lieux de détention en espaces d’apprentissage et de production pour favoriser une réinsertion sociale réussie et consolider l’autosuffisance alimentaire du Burkina Faso. À l’échelle nationale, le ministre a précisé que les superficies réellement menacées représentent environ 20 000 hectares sur l’ensemble du territoire national. Face à ces aléas climatiques localisés, Ismaël Sombié a préconisé la mobilisation de brigades d’irrigation d’urgence équipées de motopompes pour préserver les bas-fonds rizicoles. « Nous sommes venus voir la réalité sur le terrain pour nous prononcer, et non rester au bureau pendant que certains utilisent des clichés isolés pour alarmer la Nation. Notre souveraineté alimentaire se joue sur le terrain, et les résultats viendront démentir ces prédictions », a-t-il déclaré. Mettre fin à la pénurie d’eau Après le centre agricole pénitentiaire, le ministre Sombié s’est rendu sur le chantier de l’abattoir frigorifique moderne de Fada pour s’imprégner de son évolution et encourager les travailleurs à redoubler d’ardeur. Cet ouvrage a une capacité quotidienne d’abattage de 200 petits ruminants, 70 gros ruminants et 40 porcs par jour. Infrastructures intégrées, le complexe comprend, selon le représentant de l’entreprise, Jean Diarra, des unités d’abattage séparées, un bâtiment administratif, des magasins, un local de sécurité avec infirmerie, une unité de méthanisation et un éclairage intérieur solaire. Le démarrage de ce bulldozer par le ministre Sombié a marqué le lancé les travaux de l’infrastructure. " data-large-file="https://www.sidwaya.info/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/A4-1024x683.jpeg" aria-label="Ouvrez l’image en plein écran." /> Le démarrage de ce bulldozer par le ministre Sombié a marqué le lancé les travaux de l’infrastructure. Le ministre chargé de l’agriculture a exprimé sa reconnaissance aux Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS) et aux autorités locales pour la protection du chantier, soulignant le rôle stratégique de l’ouvrage pour l’approvisionnement en viande de la population et des travailleurs de la région. Il a invité l’entreprise à redoubler d’efforts pour finaliser l’infrastructure dans les délais de 10 mois qui lui sont impartis. Il a également demandé aux acteurs de la filière viande de se l’approprier et d’utiliser des camions frigorifiques afin que le transport et même l’exportation de la viande se déroulent dans de bonnes conditions hygiéniques. Le ministre Sombié a par ailleurs mis à profit sa présence dans la région pour lancer officiellement les travaux du système d’adduction d’eau potable de Fada N’Gourma. Sur le site, le ministre a assisté à la présentation technique du projet visant à résorber définitivement le déficit d’eau potable de la ville, et partant de la région. Alors que la capacité actuelle de 4 000 m³/jour (production initiale + forages d’urgence) ne permet pas de couvrir le besoin quotidien de 6 000 m³/jour, l’apport de la nouvelle station (2 200 m³/jour) permettra de combler l’intégralité du déficit et d’assurer une distribution continue au robinet, selon le secrétariat général de l’Office national de l’Eau et de l’Assainissement (ONEA), représenté par Salifou Ouédraogo. « L’ensemble du réseau sera équipé d’un système de télégestion et de commande à distance. Avec cette infrastructure, Fada ne devrait plus, en principe, connaître de pénurie en eau », a-t-il rassuré. Face au délai initialement annoncé de 10 mois par les entreprises exécutantes (Ba Hydro, EGCI), Ismaël Sombié s’est montré catégorique : « 10 mois, c’est trop long ! Nous ne pouvons pas laisser les populations affronter la période de forte chaleur (avril, mai, juin 2027) avec le même manque d’eau. Le 15 avril prochain, je viendrai moi-même pour la mise en service du système d’adduction d’eau potable de Fada. » Le ministre a aussi enjoint les autorités administratives de régler les derniers détails et a exigé un rythme de travail ininterrompu sur le chantier pour garantir le respect de cette échéance. items.title: I wouldn’t have married Simi if she were SS or AS – Adekunle Gold
items.description: Nigerian singer Adekunle Gold has revealed that genotype was a big factor for him when he wanted to marry, due to him being SS. Speaking in a recent episode of the One54 Podcast, Adekunle said he wouldn’t have married his wife if she wasn’t AA. He emphasised that it makes no sense to bring a child into the world and they would be sickly. “I wouldn’t have married my wife if she were SS or AS. Forget love. I don’t think it makes sense to bring a child into this world, and they would be sickly. “When my wife and I first met, the first thing I did was to find out her genotype. She is AA. That was why I proceeded with the relationship,” he said. Adekunle Gold has been advocating for sickle cell awareness since revealing that he is SS. He got married to fellow singer Simi in January 2019. The couple have two children.

items.title: Espace AES : Pour des frontières au service de la paix et du développement
items.description: Le Ministre d’Etat, Ministre de l’Administration territoriale et de la Mobilité, le Camarade Emile ZERBO, représentant le Premier Ministre, Chef du Gouvernement, le Camarade Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel OUEDRAOGO, a présidé, le mardi 15 septembre 2026, à Ouagadougou, la cérémonie officielle d’ouverture de la rencontre de validation et d’adoption d’un Protocole additionnel au Traité portant création de la Confédération des Etats du Sahel, relatif à la coopération transfrontalière, et d’une Décision portant institution d’un cadre de concertation transfrontalier entre les autorités administratives des régions frontalières de la Confédération des Etats du Sahel. Dans son discours, le Ministre d’Etat, Ministre de l’Administration territoriale et de la Mobilité, le Camarade Emile ZERBO, représentant le Premier Ministre, Chef du Gouvernement, a souligné que cette initiative s’inscrit pleinement dans la vision des Chefs d’Etat du Mali, du Niger et du Burkina Faso de bâtir une Confédération forte, souveraine et résolument engagée en faveur de la sécurité et du développement endogène. Pour lui, la mise en place de ce mécanisme institutionnel constitue un cadre confédéral dont l’importance n’est plus à démontrer. « Il permettra aux Gouverneurs des régions frontalières de disposer désormais d’un espace formel d’échanges, de coordination et de mutualisation de leurs ressources, de leurs efforts et de leurs actions face aux défis communs, notamment la sécurisation des zones frontalières, la lutte contre le terrorisme et la criminalité transfrontalière, la gestion concertée des ressources naturelles partagées, la facilitation de la libre circulation des personnes et des biens, la promotion du commerce et des échanges économiques entre nos territoires », a-t-il indiqué au nom du Premier Ministre. Le Ministre d’Etat, le Camarade Emile ZERBO, a, par ailleurs, appelé au renforcement de la coordination entre les autorités administratives des régions frontalières de l’espace de l’AES. Au nom du Chef du Gouvernement burkinabè, il a invité les Gouverneurs à s’approprier pleinement ce mécanisme et à en faire un outil de gouvernance de proximité, capable d’anticiper les crises, de prévenir les tensions et de promouvoir un développement harmonieux des territoires frontaliers. Pour sa part, le Ministre de l’Administration territoriale et de la Décentralisation du Mali, Porte-Parole du Gouvernement, le Général de Brigade Issa Ousmane COULIBALY, a présenté la coopération transfrontalière comme un levier essentiel pour transformer les zones frontalières de l’espace AES en véritables espaces de paix, d’intégration et de développement. « Les frontières constituent des espaces de vie et d’échanges, où les communautés entretiennent depuis des siècles des relations sociales, culturelles, économiques et familiales », a-t-il soutenu. Selon le Général de Brigade Issa Ousmane COULIBALY, le Protocole additionnel soumis à validation permettra de mieux structurer les relations entre administrations et les collectivités de part et d’autre des frontières, notamment dans les domaines du commerce, de la mobilité, de la gestion des ressources naturelles et de la prévention des conflits. Le Secrétaire Général du ministère de l’Intérieur, de la Sécurité publique et de l’Administration du Territoire du Niger, Monsieur Ayouba ABDOURAHMANE, a insisté sur la nécessité de renforcer la coopération transfrontalière afin de relever collectivement les défis sécuritaires et socio-économiques auxquels sont confrontés les Etats de la Confédération de l’AES. Il a appelé à dépasser les approches strictement nationales face aux menaces qui affectent les espaces frontaliers. « La mise en place d’un cadre de collaboration entre les autorités administratives permettra notamment de renforcer le partage de renseignements, la surveillance des zones frontalières et la coordination des opérations, tout en favorisant le développement de ces territoires », a-t-il précisé. Pour le chef de la délégation nigérienne, les deux instruments juridiques soumis aux travaux contribueront ainsi à consolider l’intégration, la solidarité et la coopération entre les trois Etats de la Confédération de l’AES. items.title: Dangote: Petrol cheaper in Nigeria than neighbours
items.description: ABUJA — President of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, has said petrol is relatively cheaper in Nigeria than in neighbouring countries, a price difference he said has continued to encourage cross-border smuggling. Dangote spoke in an interview with Arise Television on Tuesday while responding to questions about rising petrol prices in Nigeria. He said the cost of petrol should be considered in relation to prices in neighbouring countries, noting that consumers in some of those countries pay between 30 and 50 per cent more. “Expensive is relative in the sense that today, for a lot of them, there’s ignorance also. What they need to do is to ask what the neighbour’s price is,” he said. According to Dangote, the price differential creates an incentive for traders to move petrol across Nigeria’s borders for higher returns. “I don’t know if you know that there’s still a lot of smuggling of the same petrol we are producing to our neighbouring countries because those neighbouring countries are about 30 percent to 50 percent more expensive than Nigeria,” he said. He cited Niger Republic as an example, saying petrol there was about 20 to 25 per cent more expensive than in Nigeria at a domestic price of N1,350 per litre. “So what business are you going to do that will make you a 25 percent return?” he asked. Dangote said the price difference could encourage traders to divert petrol intended for domestic markets to border communities for resale. He also spoke about the potential impact of the ongoing crisis in the Middle East on energy supplies, saying availability could become a greater concern. The businessman, however, assured Nigerians that the Dangote Refinery would continue supplying the domestic market. “We will make sure that Nigeria will be fully delivered. We will deliver to Nigeria. Nigerians don’t need to worry,” he said. “There will not be any shortage from our own part. There won’t be any shortage. There will not be any queues. “And we’ll make sure that we keep satisfying the market.” The comments came after petrol prices reportedly increased at some filling stations on Monday, with prices reaching about N1,400 per litre in Lagos and N1,450 per litre in Abuja. Policy inconsistency, power supply Dangote also identified what he described as inconsistent government policies and inadequate electricity supply as major challenges facing businesses in Nigeria. “The greatest problem, there are two, which are still existing. One is inconsistencies in government policies. The second one is to do with lack of electricity,” he said. He said the cost of alternative sources of energy, particularly diesel, was putting pressure on manufacturers and making production increasingly expensive. “You cannot manufacture goods with diesel. You can see where diesel is today. You can’t even produce bread and make money today. So, we have to look at that today,” Dangote said. The businessman also highlighted Africa’s electricity access deficit, saying about 600 million people on the continent lack access to electricity. “We must make sure, even for us, really, as Africans, we cannot sit down and see that everybody is complaining. 600 million of our people, they actually don’t have power,” he said. Dangote said the scale of the electricity challenge had prompted some African business leaders to consider taking direct action to help address the continent’s power deficit. items.title: Suivi de la campagne agropastorale 2026-2027: Fada N’Gourma en voie de disposer d’un abattoir moderne de 3,5 milliards FCFA
items.description: Dans le cadre du suivi de la campagne agropastorale 2026-2027 dans la région du Goulmou, le Ministre d’État Ismaël SOMBIÉ s’est rendu le 14 septembre 2026 sur le chantier du futur abattoir moderne de Fada N’Gourma. Financé à hauteur de plus de 3,5 milliards de FCFA et affichant un taux d’exécution de 58,34 %, cet ouvrage stratégique vise à concrétiser l’initiative « Zéro exportation de bétail sur pied » en modernisant la transformation locale du bétail. Le lundi 14 septembre 2026, la visite de terrain du Ministre d’État, Ministre de l’Agriculture, de l’Eau, des Ressources animales et halieutiques, le Camarade Commandant Ismaël SOMBIÉ, a marqué une étape clé pour la région du Goulmou. Venu évaluer le déroulement de la campagne agropastorale 2026-2027, le Ministre d'État a inspecté l'état d'avancement des travaux de construction du nouvel abattoir moderne de Fada N’Gourma. Ce projet s'inscrit directement dans la feuille de route gouvernementale de l’« Offensive agropastorale, hydraulique et halieutique 2026-2028 », sous-tendue par l’opération spéciale « Zéro exportation de bétail sur pied ». L'objectif affiché est de limiter l'exportation brute des animaux afin de privilégier la transformation industrielle et la valorisation de la production animale sur le territoire national. Sur le terrain, le projet commence à dévoiler son architecture industrielle. Avec un coût global estimé à plus de 3,5 milliards de FCFA, l'ouvrage enregistre actuellement un taux d’exécution physique de 58,34 %. Une fois achevé, le complexe disposera d'une capacité prévisionnelle de traitement quotidien de 70 bovins, 200 petits ruminants et 40 porcs. Pour atteindre ce rythme industriel, le site accueillera un ensemble complet d'équipements : un bâtiment administratif, des parcs de stabulation adaptés aux différentes espèces, des quais de débarquement, des magasins, une infirmerie et une cafétéria. Les installations prévoient également une unité complète d’abattage pour bovins et ovins-caprins, une ligne dédiée aux porcs, un système de traitement et de gestion des déchets, ainsi qu'une machine destinée à la fabrication de compost. L'autonomie et la sécurité du site seront garanties par un poste d’eau autonome, un groupe électrogène et un dispositif de vidéosurveillance. L'avancement actuel des travaux suscite la satisfaction des autorités, d'autant que le chantier a imposé des contraintes logistiques particulières. Contrairement à d'autres projets s'appuyant sur des infrastructures existantes à réhabiliter, le chantier de Fada N’Gourma a dû démarrer pratiquement de zéro. Face à ce défi majeur, le Ministre d’État a tenu à saluer la synergie entre les acteurs civils et sécuritaires : l'engagement des autorités administratives et locales, des entreprises adjudicataires et des équipes techniques s'est combiné à l'accompagnement des Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS) pour sécuriser et maintenir la dynamique des travaux. Pour les acteurs de la région, cette infrastructure ne se résume pas à un simple alignement de murs et d'équipements. Elle a été pensée pour devenir un véritable moteur économique pour toute la chaîne de valeur bétail-viande du Goulmou. En garantissant le respect des normes actuelles en matière d’hygiène et de sécurité sanitaire des aliments, l'abattoir entend protéger la santé des consommateurs tout en créant de la valeur ajoutée au profit des éleveurs, des commerçants et des transformateurs locaux. Tout au long de sa visite, le Ministre d’État a réitéré son exigence de rigueur, rappelant que le suivi du chantier se poursuivra activement jusqu’à la livraison finale afin de s'assurer de la parfaite conformité de l'ouvrage livré avec le projet initial. items.title: 3 000 francs CFA et saisie du véhicule : Le prix du non-respect du casque dès le 1er octobre
items.description: À l'approche de la rentrée scolaire 2026, le ministère de la Sécurité du Burkina Faso met un terme à la tolérance administrative concernant le port du casque de protection. Dès le 1er octobre 2026, tout conducteur d'engin motorisé à deux ou trois roues circulant sans casque s'exposera à une amende de 3 000 francs CFA et à l'immobilisation immédiate de son véhicule. À l'approche de la rentrée des classes, la circulation routière connaît une hausse d'intensité qui accroît le risque d'accidents sur le réseau routier. Face à ce constat, le ministre de la Sécurité, le Camarade Mahamadou SANA, a signé ce 15 septembre 2026 un communiqué officiel rappelant le respect impératif des règles de circulation, en particulier l'obligation du port du casque. Tout en félicitant la majorité de la population qui a déjà adopté cet équipement de protection, le ministère entend désormais étendre cette discipline à l'ensemble des usagers. Jusqu'ici, les conducteurs en infraction bénéficiaient d'une période de tolérance administrative durant laquelle les forces de contrôle se limitaient à des actions de sensibilisation et au refoulement des contrevenants sans leur infliger d'amende. Cette période pédagogique prendra fin le 1er octobre 2026. À compter de cette date, l'obligation du port du casque fera l'objet d'une application stricte et sans exception pour tout conducteur de deux ou trois-roues motorisé. En cas d'infraction, les usagers subiront les sanctions prévues par la réglementation, à savoir une amende de 3 000 francs CFA assortie de l'immobilisation de l'engin jusqu'à la présentation d'un casque de protection conforme. Afin d'assurer le respect strict de cette directive, les services compétents ont reçu l'instruction de déployer des contrôles rigoureux sur l'ensemble du territoire. À travers cette mesure, les autorités comptent sur la responsabilité collective et la collaboration citoyenne pour préserver des vies humaines, notamment celles des élèves et étudiants, en cette nouvelle année scolaire. items.title: Police, experts meet on 2027 election security
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigeria Police Force (NPF) is set to host the sixth Conference and Retreat for Senior Police Officers (CARSPO 2026) in Imo State from September 21 to 24, with election security expected to feature prominently in discussions ahead of the 2027 general elections. The conference, themed “Developing a Police Roadmap for Effective Management of Security During Elections,” is expected to bring together senior police officers, security experts, policymakers, election stakeholders and representatives of relevant institutions to review election security arrangements and identify emerging challenges. CARSPO 2026 is being organised by the Nigeria Police Force in partnership with Lenders Consult International. According to the organisers, discussions at the four-day conference will focus on the development of a security roadmap for the 2027 elections, with issues including election-related violence, intelligence gathering, inter-agency cooperation, deployment strategies, technology in election policing and public confidence in the electoral process. Senior police officers from across the country, representatives of government agencies, civil society organisations, election management bodies, development partners and security experts are expected to participate. The organisers said the conference would provide an opportunity for stakeholders to assess existing approaches to election security and consider measures for improving coordination and operational preparedness before, during and after elections. Lenders Consult International also reaffirmed its partnership with the Nigeria Police Force, saying it had worked with the Force since 2019 on sponsorship and operational support initiatives. Ahead of the conference, the organisers said proactive planning, training and inter-agency coordination remained important to election security, given the range of security challenges that can arise during electoral activities. The Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, is expected to lead discussions at the conference and provide strategic direction on the Force’s preparations for future electoral engagements. Disu stressed the role of the police in maintaining security during elections. “Stability of the electoral process largely depends on the Police as the lead agency in internal democracy,” the IGP stated. He also emphasised the responsibility of the Force to provide a secure environment for the conduct of elections. The organisers said recommendations from CARSPO 2026 would inform the Nigeria Police Force’s preparations and operational planning for election security ahead of the 2027 general elections. items.title: FG Commissions KWASU ICT Centre for Youths
items.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin The Federal Government has commissioned a TETFund/Renewed Hope Initiative-backed ICT Experience Centre at the Kwara State University (KWASU), Malete, to equip Nigerian youths with digital skills needed to thrive in a modern and competitive world. Wife of the President, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, who was represented at the commissioning on Tuesday by the wife of the Vice-President, Nana Shettima, said the initiative aligned with the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration, particularly its focus on youth empowerment, education, innovation and economic transformation. She said the President was committed to creating opportunities that would equip Nigerian youths with the knowledge and skills required to compete in a rapidly changing world. According to her, the ICT Experience Centre was a testament to the Federal Government’s commitment to advancing education, promoting digital inclusion and enhancing graduate employability. “The TETFund/Renewed Hope Initiative ICT Experience Centre we are commissioning today represents opportunity, innovation, knowledge and the future of young people in Kwara State and beyond,” she said. She explained that the facility was designed as a modern technology centre equipped with an ICT laboratory, interactive digital displays, conference facilities and exhibition spaces to provide an environment for learning, creativity, research and technological advancement. KWASU is one of six tertiary institutions selected for the pilot phase of the intervention, with one institution representing each of the country’s six geopolitical zones. Tinubu said similar centres had been commissioned at Ekiti State University on May 28, University of Cross River State on September 4 and Anambra State Polytechnic on September 10. She added that the centres at Kaduna State University and Taraba State University would be commissioned soon. According to her, the next phase of the intervention would cover 15 institutions in Adamawa, Bayelsa, Borno, Delta, Edo, Enugu, Imo, Katsina, Nasarawa, Niger, Ondo, Osun, Rivers, Yobe and Zamfara states, where construction is ongoing. She said the expansion demonstrated the administration’s commitment to ensuring that more Nigerian youths, regardless of their locations, had access to digital learning opportunities. Tinubu urged students to take ownership of the facility, maximise the opportunities it provides and use technology positively to improve their lives, communities and the nation. Earlier, Kwara State Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq said his administration’s vision was to ensure that every young person in the state acquired the skills and opportunities needed to succeed in a changing world. He urged the university management to make judicious use of the facility, saying it should support students and help generate innovations, businesses, jobs and sustainable solutions to challenges facing communities. “Technology and digital skills now shape how we learn, work and create opportunities. Our young people must, therefore, have access to the skills and techniques they need to compete anywhere in Nigeria and across the world,” AbdulRazaq said. The governor said his administration would continue to invest in education and human capital development. He noted that the state had expanded KWASU into a multi-campus institution, with the completion of its Osi and Ilesha Baruba campuses, while plans were underway for another campus in Ajase-Ipo. Also speaking, the Executive Secretary of TETFund, Architect Sonny Echono, said the centres were being established across selected universities, polytechnics and colleges of education, with KWASU hosting the facility for the North-Central zone. He said the initiative was designed to enhance graduate employability, foster innovation and position Nigeria to participate more effectively in the global technology-driven economy through practical training and digital skills acquisition. Echono said the ICT Experience Centre would equip students and lecturers with critical digital skills in areas including artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, robotics and software development. “The centre being commissioned today is one of the foremost ICT Experience Centres being delivered across the country, and the third to be commissioned this year,” he said. He added that the facility was equipped with modern digital devices, computer systems and relevant software to facilitate training, practical learning and skills development. The centre, according to him, was also furnished and fully air-conditioned, with supporting power and municipal infrastructure. The Vice-Chancellor of KWASU, Prof. Shaykh-Luqman Jimoh, described the facility as an investment in human capital, innovation, entrepreneurship and the future of Nigeria. He said the centre would provide students with opportunities to develop practical digital skills and engage with contemporary technologies, while also serving as a hub for interdisciplinary engagement. “The centre represents vision, belief and an investment in the Nigerian youth to better shape the future of our nation,” Jimoh said. The post FG Commissions KWASU ICT Centre for Youths appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Meta’s Zuckerberg says AI labs have enough incentive to build safely
items.description: Meta platform CEO Mark Zuckerberg said on Tuesday that competition and liability give AI companies enough reason to act individually ‌on safety, appearing to break from calls by leaders of top AI firms for a coordinated slowdown in AI development. The comments underscore a split among industry executives and U.S. authorities over how to respond to warnings that the technology is advancing faster than companies can control it, with some industry insiders warning ​it poses an existential threat to humanity . The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here. Zuckerberg, in an X post on Tuesday, said that every lab has the responsibility ​and incentive to move at the pace required to train its models safely, and the ability to ⁠take its own actions to ensure that happens. His remarks come three days after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei urged AI companies to slow ​the pace at which they improve model capabilities, on the heels of existential risk warnings by several researchers. Rival OpenAI’s chief Sam Altman and xAI’s ​Elon Musk both publicly endorsed Amodei’s call within hours. ADMINISTRATION PUSHBACK ON AI REGULATION, SLOWDOWN President Donald Trump on Monday, however, downplayed concerns about AI’s potential for harm, saying the U.S. already had guardrails in place for the technology and that China would benefit from doubt being cast on AI’s development. The view that regulations will ​harm U.S. companies’ ability to compete with their Chinese counterparts is shared by tech executives, including Nvidia (NVDA.O), opens new tab CEO Jensen Huang . “Trust and alignment are ​quickly becoming the most important capabilities that will differentiate agents and models,” Zuckerberg said Tuesday. “Any lab that doesn’t focus on alignment will fall behind.” Zuckerberg also ‌said Tuesday ⁠that labs had a strong incentive to prevent their models from causing harm as they would face “significant” liability otherwise. He pointed to Meta delaying the release of its Muse AI agent earlier this year to strengthen its security. “We didn’t call for everyone else to do this before we would. We just did it as part of our day-to-day work because it was clearly the right thing for people and ​for us,” he said. INDEPENDENT EVALUATORS “INDUSTRY ​BEST PRACTICE” While Amodei called for ⁠an industry-wide slowing of recursive self-improvement — AI’s ability to improve itself — Zuckerberg said Meta had already committed the “significant majority” of its compute toward creating products that serve users’ immediate needs rather than pursuing self-improving ​AI systems. Zuckerberg also said Meta Superintelligence Labs — its AI division — already engaged independent evaluators in several ​areas, calling it “industry best ⁠practice” and that “other labs can just do this too”. Zuckerberg’s push to position Meta as a responsible actor on AI safety comes weeks after the company agreed to pay up to $18 billion to settle U.S. state lawsuits alleging it designed Facebook and Instagram to addict children, without admitting wrongdoing. Adding ⁠to the ​uncertainty around any coordinated approach by AI firms, FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson said Tuesday ​everyone should be “ deeply suspicious ” of AI companies seeking antitrust exemptions while lobbying for new regulations. While Ferguson did not name Anthropic, Amodei last week requested antitrust permission to enable ​rivals to coordinate a slower pace to AI development due to safety concerns.

items.title: Higher SSB Tax may raise prices – Report warns
items.description: By Chidinma Chukwu, ABUJA A new report by ThinkBusiness Africa has warned that the proposed increase in Nigeria’s excise duty on sugar-sweetened beverages (SSBs) could significantly raise prices of soft drinks, while its impact on obesity, diabetes and hypertension remains uncertain. The report examined the proposed amendment to the Customs, Excise Tariff, Etc. (Consolidation) Act (CETA), which seeks to replace the existing N10-per-litre excise duty with an ad valorem tax. According to the report, the proposed system could raise the effective tax burden to about N130 per litre based on prevailing beverage prices. It said the change would make taxation dependent on the value of beverages rather than the volume produced, potentially increasing prices and placing additional administrative pressure on manufacturers. Citing modelling by the Centre for the Study of the Economies of Africa (CSEA), as referenced in a submission by the Manufacturers Association of Nigeria, ThinkBusiness Africa said a N130-per-litre tax could result in a 39 per cent increase in retail prices and a 29 per cent reduction in annual per capita consumption of SSBs. It also projected that annual industry output could decline from N1.5 trillion to N1.1 trillion by 2030, while the production index could fall from 78 to about 40. The report, however, stressed that the figures were modelled scenarios and did not represent observed outcomes. On the public health implications, ThinkBusiness Africa acknowledged evidence that taxes on SSBs could reduce purchases of taxed beverages, but said evidence was less conclusive on whether such reductions would translate into lower rates of obesity, diabetes and hypertension. “Chronic diseases are influenced by several factors, including overall diet, physical activity, income, education and access to healthcare,” the report said. It also questioned the proposed use of beverage value as the basis for the tax, arguing that a levy directly linked to sugar content could better achieve the health objective. The report cited South Africa and the United Kingdom, where sugar-related taxes are linked to sugar content or specified thresholds, saying such systems could encourage manufacturers to reformulate products and reduce sugar levels. ThinkBusiness Africa said more than 133 million Nigerians were living in multidimensional poverty, with households already facing weak purchasing power and rising living costs. “For many households, the immediate effect of a higher SSB tax will be straightforward: higher prices. “For manufacturers, distributors and retailers, the consequences may include higher costs, weaker demand and pressure on production. This matters because the beverage sector is not an isolated industry. It is connected to agriculture, sugar supply, packaging, logistics, transportation, wholesale and retail,” it said. The report also cited data from the National Sugar Development Council showing that total sugar consumption fell from about 1.72 million tonnes in 2022 to 1.44 million tonnes in 2023, while domestic production dropped from 46,479 tonnes to 30,053 tonnes. Although the declines could not be attributed solely to the existing SSB tax, the report said they reflected a difficult operating environment characterised by inflation, exchange-rate pressures, rising input costs and weaker consumer demand. It further warned that a higher tax would not necessarily guarantee increased or sustainable government revenue, as reduced consumption, lower formal-sector production and a shift to informal markets could shrink the taxable base. ThinkBusiness Africa therefore called for a comprehensive assessment of the proposed tax, greater transparency on revenue generated from the existing N10-per-litre levy and consideration of a sugar-content-based tax. It also recommended stronger non-tax measures, including public health campaigns, promotion of physical activity, early screening for diabetes and hypertension, and improved primary healthcare. The report said Nigeria needed stronger measures to tackle diabetes, obesity and hypertension, but cautioned that a substantially higher SSB tax should not automatically be equated with an effective public health policy. items.title: Messi in Argentina squad for farewell friendly
items.description: Argentina have named Lionel Messi in their squad for a friendly against Benin in October in a match which is set to be the forward’s farewell to international football. Messi announced his retirement from Argentina duty in August, following his country’s defeat to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final and after saying he was considering his future in football after the death of his father, Jorge. The 39-year-old, who captained Argentina when they won the 2022 World Cup, said the decision to stop playing for La Albiceleste hurt him “deeply” but that he had “given it my all” and had “nothing left to give”. Messi, an eight-time Ballon d’Or winner who currently plays for Inter Miami, is Argentina’s all-time leading scorer and most-capped player, having scored 125 goals in 207 appearances. “We made the decision to invite the best player in the world, the symbol of our national team, our captain, Lionel Andres Messi, so that he can have the farewell he truly deserves on 6 October here in Argentina,” said Argentine FA president Claudio Tapia. River Plate’s Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires, with a capacity of 85,000, will host the game against Benin. Argentina’s 2022 World Cup winners have also been invited to the match, which Tapia said would be an “unforgettable” occasion. Argentina were ordered to play their next two home matches with 50% capacity, although one match of that sanction was suspended, for breaches of the FIFA disciplinary code during the World Cup. The punishment relates to using a sporting event for non-sporting demonstrations, team misconduct, and discriminatory chants and gestures by its supporters. After defeating England 2-1 in the World Cup semi-final, several Argentina players held up a banner claiming Argentine sovereignty over the Falkland Islands, a British overseas territory. As they play friendlies against Bolivia on 30 September in Cordoba and against Burkina Faso on 3 October in Buenos Aires, it should mean the punishment will have been served before the Benin game. Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes and team-mate Nahuel Molina are not expected to be available as they were given respective 10-game and seven-match suspensions for their part in on-field clashes following their country’s defeat by Spain in the World Cup final.

items.title: Argentine – Burkina Faso : Lionel Messi attendu face aux Etalons le 3 octobre à Buenos Aires
items.description: Dans le cadre de la fenêtre FIFA d'octobre 2026, la Fédération Burkinabè de Football et la Fédération Argentine de Football ont officiellement confirmé la tenue d’une rencontre amicale inédite entre les Étalons du Burkina Faso et l’Albiceleste, le 3 octobre prochain à Buenos Aires. Inséré dans une série de matchs internationaux qui marquera les adieux de Lionel Messi à la sélection argentine, ce rendez-vous offre un défi sportif d'envergure au football burkinabè. C'est un dénouement majeur pour la diplomatie sportive et les supporters des deux nations. Après une première publication le 4 septembre suivie d'un retrait temporaire lié aux clauses de confidentialité contractuelles, la Fédération Burkinabè de Football (FBF) et son homologue argentine (AFA) ont acté une annonce conjointe le mardi 15 septembre 2026 à 16h00 GMT. La FBF a ainsi formalisé l'information à 16h26 sur ses canaux officiels : les Étalons du Burkina Faso affronteront bel et bien l'Argentine en match amical international le 3 octobre 2026 à Buenos Aires. Pour l’Albiceleste, dirigée par Lionel Scaloni, ce choc face aux Étalons s'inscrit au cœur d'un triptyque de rencontres à domicile programmées entre le 30 septembre et le 6 octobre 2026. Les champions du monde en titre débuteront leur tournée le 30 septembre face à la Bolivie à Córdoba, avant de rejoindre le stade El Monumental pour croiser le fer avec le Burkina Faso le 3 octobre, puis le Bénin le 6 octobre. Cette trêve internationale revêt une dimension émotionnelle historique. Selon la Fédération argentine et la presse internationale (TV5Monde, ESPN), le sélectionneur Lionel Scaloni a inclus Lionel Messi dans son groupe afin de lui offrir un jubilé devant son public. Après avoir annoncé sa retraite internationale fin août à 39 ans, l'octuple Ballon d'Or honorera son ultime sélection le 6 octobre face au Bénin devant 85 000 spectateurs, clôturant une carrière légendaire de 207 sélections et 125 buts sous le maillot argentin. Pour les Étalons du Burkina Faso (62e au classement FIFA), ce déplacement dans la capitale argentine représente un test de maturité exceptionnel. Après avoir croisé la Russie et la Biélorussie lors de la fenêtre FIFA de juin dernier, la sélection burkinabè s'offre une confrontation inédite en équipe sénior face à l'Albiceleste. Si les deux nations s'étaient déjà rencontrées en 2001 lors de la finale de la Coupe du monde des moins de 20 ans sur le sol argentin, cette première grande affiche internationale constitue une vitrine mondiale de premier ordre pour les Étalons du Burkina Faso. items.title: OpenAI boss says world ‘right to be afraid’ but ‘should trust’ AI firms
items.description: OpenAI boss Sam Altman thinks people should have more faith in his company and others like it to do the right thing when it comes to artificial intelligence (AI) development amid rising public concerns about all the risks. “The world should trust that we are going to do the right thing because it’s the right thing and we feel the magnitude of this,” Altman said on Tuesday during a conference in San Francisco. However, Altman noted that people were justified in their fears about AI, as the capabilities of the tools have progressed rapidly. “It doesn’t take as much imagination as it used to for [us] to imagine how this could go wrong,” he said. “I think the world is right to be afraid of this.” Altman’s comments came during an appearance at an annual conference hosted by software firm Salesforce. It was the first time he had spoken publicly since a post went viral last week by a researcher who quit the AI firm Anthropic. The researcher claimed AI could kill all humans by the end of the decade if left unchecked. A handful of other AI executives and experts responded by saying they agreed with the assessment, though they didn’t explain how they came to their conclusions or how exactly AI could accomplish such a thing. The fervor over the claims has led to more scrutiny of AI development in recent days, and in response, Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei called for the pace of all AI development to slow and urged governments to regulate the industry. The post was applauded by Altman, as well as co-founder of Google’s DeepMind Demis Hassabis, and Elon Musk, owner of social media site X and AI assistant Grok. By Tuesday, more AI leaders were voicing support for self-regulation rather than government involvement . Altman said that he felt AI companies like his own were capable of essentially regulating themselves. “We will get it right, I’m very confident in our company’s and industry’s ability to do this safely,” Altman said, adding that he was sure that they would “keep alignment and safety way ahead of capabilities” and if they couldn’t, they would “slow down or stop”. After Altman’s comments, Meta boss Mark Zuckerberg wrote on X that every AI lab has the ability and the incentive “to take its own actions” towards making AI tools and models that are designed for safety. “Any lab that doesn’t focus on alignment will fall behind,” Zuckerberg wrote. “Labs face significant liability if their models cause harm, so they have a strong incentive to prevent this as well.” Jensen Huang, head of Nvidia, also said at the same Tuesday conference that the AI firms should decide if new versions of the technology should be released and not be managed by outside forces. “We don’t need new laws or regulations,” Huang said, adding that there should not be a “false choice” between the speed of innovation and the safety of AI products. Nvidia is the biggest company in the world by valuation, with its profits having boomed as a result of rampant demand for the AI computing chips it makes. “Safety is paramount. However, safety is an engineering problem,” Huang said. He added that if at any time a leader of an AI company lacks confidence in their product they should choose to not release it. “That’s a very obvious thing to do,” Huang said. “Run as fast as you can, but if at any time you feel the institution is not in control, take a pause.” Some industry figures have argued resurgent AI fears were overblown and were being jumped on to generate hype for the industry. During the conference, Altman addressed a crowd of hundreds of business people, telling them they should use AI tools to aid in their work, but also needed them in order to protect their businesses from potentially AI-enabled cyber attacks. The idea of AI executives being left to entirely regulate themselves has struck some in the industry as a bad idea. Jack Clark, an Anthropic executive and co-founder, told the BBC on Monday that leaving AI to be a “totally unregulated industry” was “rolling dice with immense risks” . Patrick Hillman, the chief operating officer of Logical Intelligence, which is chaired by Yann LeCun, a sage of the AI industry, noted Tuesday how little faith people have in tech companies to do anything truly in the public interest . “The only institution that Americans might trust less than Washington these days is Silicon Valley. I have worked and lived in both and I assure you both have earned this scepticism,” Hillman said. “If you believe what you are building is dangerous, show us what you are prepared to stop doing,” he added. Leaders of OpenAI and Anthropic have said they have recently started working towards some sort of industry-wide agreement on safety. Amodei, during a cameo at the conference on Tuesday, said Anthropic is now in “a dialogue with the rest of the industry” about committing to better safety standards and checks on AI tools and development. He also said that one of the biggest surprises of the AI boom was not how the technology itself has advanced, but its broader impact. “We didn’t appreciate that it would lead to companies growing so fast, and how quickly they would become central to things,” Amodei said. OpenAI executive Chris Lehane said last week that the company was also working with other AI labs “to advance frontier AI standards, building a voluntary effort now, with or without government support.” Those labs include Anthropic and Google Deepmind. “With stakes this high, we cannot let the perfect become the enemy of the good,” Lehane wrote.

items.title: Nigeria: Une mère arrêtée pour abus sexuels filmés sur ses enfants contre rémunération
items.description: La police de l’État d’Anambra a annoncé le 10 septembre l’arrestation d’Anulika Onyeanusia, 36 ans, soupçonnée d’avoir sexuellement abusé sa fille, âgée de sept ans, et d’avoir diffusé ce contenu en ligne contre rémunération. L’affaire a éclaté après la mise en ligne d’une vidéo montrant des faits d’abus, qui a rapidement circulé sur les réseaux sociaux et provoqué une vague d’indignation au Nigeria. Selon le porte-parole de la police, le commissaire Tochukwu Ikenga, les enquêteurs ont exploité des renseignements collectés en source ouverte pour localiser la suspecte à Onitsha. L’opération a permis de secourir quatre enfants âgés de deux à neuf ans placés sous sa garde, ainsi que de saisir plusieurs objets retenus comme éléments de preuve. Le mari de la suspecte est également entendu par les enquêteurs, qui cherchent à déterminer si d’autres personnes ont pu être impliquées. Interrogée, Anulika Onyeanusia aurait reconnu avoir perçu jusqu’à 300 dollars d’un client basé à l’étranger en échange de ce contenu, avant d’attribuer ses actes à ce qu’elle a qualifié d’« œuvre du diable ». Le commissaire de police de l’État d’Anambra, Nnanna Oji Ama, a qualifié les faits allégués d’inacceptables et ordonné une enquête approfondie, en insistant sur la priorité donnée à la sécurité et à la prise en charge psychologique des enfants secourus. Cette affaire relance, au-delà du seul cas d’Onitsha, la question de l’exploitation d’enfants africains par des réseaux de sollicitation en ligne opérant depuis l’étranger, où des internautes proposent des rémunérations en devises fortes contre du contenu impliquant des mineurs, souvent via des plateformes de diffusion en direct peu ou pas modérées. Plusieurs organisations de protection de l’enfance nigérianes ont appelé à un renforcement de la coopération entre plateformes numériques et forces de l’ordre pour identifier plus rapidement ce type de contenu. L’enquête se poursuit et la suspecte reste en garde à vue. D’autres développements sont attendus, notamment sur d’éventuelles poursuites contre le ou les clients impliqués dans la sollicitation de ce contenu. L’article Nigeria: Une mère arrêtée pour abus sexuels filmés sur ses enfants contre rémunération est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: UK in talks about joining global defence bank led by Canada
items.description: The UK government is in discussions about joining a global investment bank, aimed at raising more money for defence spending. Chancellor John Healey is considering a bid to join the Defence, Security and Resilience Bank (DSRB), not long after his predecessor Rachel Reeves rejected the idea. Canada has been leading efforts to establish the bank, which supporters say would enable governments to borrow at lower costs to increase military spending. Treasury officials stressed that no decision has been made. A government spokesperson said it was “fully committed to working alongside our international partners to scale defence industrial capacity.” Before he cancelled commitments due to the death of his father, Prime Minister Andy Burnham had been due to meet Canada’s Prime Minister Mark Carney in the UK on Wednesday. Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte is also travelling to the UK for his first meeting with the prime minister. He is giving a speech in Oxfordshire, where he is expected to say the UK is “serious about security” and praise the country’s efforts supporting Ukraine. He will also say that Nato will “not be intimidated by Russia’s campaign of hostile actions. “Russia wants to stop us helping Ukraine – but their actions will only lead us to do more for Ukraine.” It comes after Nato forces shot down a drone over Lithuania in the latest security scare on the alliance’s eastern flank, where tensions remain high amid Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. And on Tuesday Denmark also accused a Russian warship of firing two emergency flares at one of its helicopters while it was tracking the vessel in the Baltic Sea. Cheaper loans for defence projects The DSRB is a multilateral bank aimed at providing cheaper loans to fund defence projects and has backing from Albania, Bulgaria, Belgium, Greece, Latvia, Luxembourg, Romania, Turkey and Ukraine. Membership of the bank for the UK and other G7 countries would come with an upfront investment cost of around £870m spread over three years. Paying for the UK’s growing defence commitments is one of Healey’s biggest headaches as he prepares for the Budget in October and next year’s spending review. The government has so far avoided committing to raising defence spending to 3% of national income by 2030, only repeating the longer term goal of 3.5% by 2035. As defence secretary, Healey privately pushed for the UK to join the DSRB as a means of raising money. He resigned in June, accusing the Treasury of being unwilling to provide the resources needed to defend the country. In his resignation letter, he said there were “credible ways” to fund extra defence spending, including “working multinationally”. A government spokesperson said: “We are fully committed to working alongside our international partners to scale defence industrial capacity. “We are working closely with our Canadian allies on ensuring the Multilateral Defence Mechanism and Defence Security Resilience Bank are complementary.”

items.title: The Only Thing Capable of Uniting Bernie and Bannon
items.description: I f there was any question over whether the concept of “the enemy of my enemy is my friend” is still operative in Washington’s hyper-partisan political environment, the answer may be found in the budding coalition of progressives and MAGA-friendly activists who have united in recent days to speak out against artificial intelligence. Which is how Senator Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon found themselves speaking on the same stage today. With warnings that the technology could cause mass economic displacement and even human extinction, political figures who once wanted nothing to do with one another are suddenly joining forces, scrambling the political landscape just weeks before the midterm elections. The odd couples, who would have been hard to fathom just weeks ago, are also reshaping the legislative agenda. Republican Senators Ted Cruz and John Thune have teamed up with Democratic Senator Amy Klobuchar on an AI-safety bill; progressive Senator Richard Blumenthal joined forces with conservative Senator Josh Hawley to push a bill requiring AI companies to obtain approval from the Department of Energy before deploying new systems. Nearly a decade ago, Sanders urged then-President-Elect Trump to reverse his decision to hire Bannon, a pugilistic architect of the MAGA movement, and called him “a racist individual.” Last year, Bannon called Sanders a “pussy” for not going after Hillary Clinton hard enough in 2016. But the two were able to put all of that aside today to deliver the same message: If AI has the potential to wipe out humanity, Americans should have a say in how it operates. [ Read: Trump’s see-no-evil AI policy ] “If the lives of every man, woman, and child are going to be fundamentally changed by this technology, then the people of this country must make the decisions about AI, and not just a handful of oligarchs,” Sanders said at the all-day “Pro-Human Assembly.” Bannon sounded pretty much exactly the same. “The American citizens are not going to be supplicants to the oligarchs anymore,” the MAGA strategist said in what easily could have been a continuation of the Vermont socialist’s remarks. “We can’t do it.” Standing decidedly outside of this spirit of cross-party cooperation is Trump, who has downplayed warnings about AI’s risks and called the concerns over the rapidly advancing technology a “hoax.” Trump made a surprise appearance at an AI-friendly event yesterday by placing a phone call to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and making clear that he does not believe the doomsday warnings that have circulated in recent days. “The robots are not going to be taking over the world,” he told Huang, who took the call while speaking at a summit in Los Angeles and put it on speakerphone for the crowd to hear. “That’s not going to happen.” Bannon and Sanders, speaking back-to-back, essentially agreed to disagree about Trump. Sanders said that Trump’s “ignorance regarding this issue is truly embarrassing” and suggested that the president is not taking the technology’s risks seriously enough. “Obviously, he and I have a quite different opinion of the president of the United States,” Bannon told the crowd. “But we’re trying to raise above partisanship, and we have to.” That line received applause. But overriding Trump’s opposition to AI regulation in order to make meaningful policy changes could be a heavy lift. In several social-media posts yesterday, Trump dismissed those concerned about AI’s dangers as “Conspiracy Theorists, Treasonists, Traitors, and Leakers.” He suggested that AI and the data centers that power it could represent the greatest economic opportunity in American history. “Don’t kill the Golden Goose!” he wrote. Some lawmakers and activists, including Trump supporters and detractors, are now attempting to create a formal coalition to push for stronger guardrails around AI. Sanders plans to host a closed-door, bipartisan briefing on AI tomorrow in Washington. Today’s event in Washington was branded by organizers as an opportunity to create a “more human-centric path for AI development.” Speakers, including lawmakers, labor officials, and faith leaders, leaned heavily on the idea that the battle to slow AI’s advance should transcend traditional partisan or ideological divides. [ Ian Bogost: The thrill of wanting AI to destroy the world ] The event was organized by the Future of Life Institute, a nonprofit that was primarily funded by a donation of more than $650 million in 2021 from Vitalik Buterin, a wealthy cryptocurrency entrepreneur. (The donation was delivered in crypto.) Politico reported in 2024 that the small organization’s hefty war chest put it in the same league as organizational behemoths such as the American Civil Liberties Union Foundation and the Brookings Institution. Today’s event featured free merch that included Carhartt shirts, yellow hoodies, and camouflage hats featuring mottos such as Keep the future human and Pro-Human. A video booth, fully decked out with stage lighting and a single chair, offered attendees the chance to answer the prompt When did you feel most human? Not, apparently, on video: When I walked by it a few times, it was not being used. A parody news report on nearby television screens played a staged interview with “Dan X,” who appeared to be a stand-in for an AI executive. The CEO of a fictional company called Replacement.AI was described by the faux journalist as “a walking paradox” who “loves people but isn’t crazy about humans.” Wearing a Patagonia vest and a smartwatch, the Millennial-coded CEO ended the interview by offering this advice: “Live every day as if it is your last, because one day soon, very soon, it might be.” Stuart Russell, a computer-science professor and the president of the International Association for Safe & Ethical AI, told the crowd that his private discussions with AI-company officials included even more dire predictions about the technology’s dangers than what they have discussed publicly. But organizers seemed eager to push the event beyond dystopian warnings and move toward solutions. “There is no better testimony to how united we are than the mind-blowing ideological diversity that you’re going to see onstage today,” Max Tegmark, a co-founder and the chair of the Future of Life Institute, said at the assembly’s opening. In addition to lawmakers, the event featured clergy who spoke about AI’s impact on faith, parents whose teenage children had committed suicide after engaging with chatbots, and economists concerned about the mass displacement of the workforce. Attendees attempting to navigate the event website had to first agree to “Standards of Conduct” requiring participants to “practice active listening” and refrain from personal attacks. Representative Chip Roy of Texas, who is retiring from Congress, was the only elected Republican to appear onstage. He told me that organizers had encouraged him to avoid politics in his remarks but that he predicted that political differences will inevitably intrude as the debate over what to do about AI continues. “I doubt Bernie’s solutions are going to be my solution,” he said. Still, there were signs that figures on both sides of the aisle seemed ready to at least have an honest conversation. “I don’t think you could find any two harder partisans than Bernie Sanders on the left and Steve Bannon on the right,” Bannon said during his remarks. “This is a hinge in history. We have to handle this correctly. To handle it correctly, No. 1, we can never trust what an oligarch says.” Sanders was by then out of sight, but on that much, he surely agreed.

items.title: ONU : l’IA au cœur des débats face aux risques pour l’humanité
items.description: L’intelligence artificielle devrait occuper une place centrale dans les discussions internationales la semaine prochaine. À l’occasion de l’Assemblée générale des Nations unies, le Conseil de sécurité devrait consacrer une réunion aux risques liés au développement rapide de cette technologie, notamment à ceux que certains experts qualifient désormais de potentiellement existentiels pour l’humanité. L’initiative intervient alors que les mises en garde se multiplient concernant les systèmes d’intelligence artificielle les plus avancés. Selon une source diplomatique française citée par l’AFP, le sujet sera « très haut dans l’agenda » de l’Assemblée générale. La perspective d’une discussion internationale sur les dangers de l’IA intervient toutefois dans un contexte de profond désaccord aux États-Unis. L’administration de Donald Trump s’oppose à une réglementation jugée trop contraignante, estimant qu’elle pourrait affaiblir la position américaine dans la compétition technologique avec la Chine. Le président américain a récemment rejeté les avertissements concernant une éventuelle menace existentielle liée à l’IA, allant jusqu’à dénoncer une « conspiration malsaine » autour de cette question. Une position également défendue par le président républicain de la Chambre des représentants, Mike Johnson. Celui-ci estime qu’une accélération du processus législatif pourrait nuire à la compétitivité américaine face à Pékin. « Si le Congrès se hâte et convoque une session extraordinaire pour essayer de réguler l’IA, nous allons perdre la course contre la Chine » , a-t-il déclaré, appelant les élus à ne pas « étouffer l’innovation ». Au Congrès, le débat est cependant loin d’être clos. Alors que les élus américains ont repris leurs travaux sur la régulation de l’intelligence artificielle le 14 septembre, plusieurs responsables démocrates réclament des mesures plus ambitieuses. Le chef de la minorité démocrate au Sénat, Chuck Schumer, souhaite notamment organiser une réunion d’information classifiée consacrée aux risques liés à l’IA. « Les signaux d’alarme retentissent plus fort que jamais, et l’administration Trump détourne le regard » , a-t-il déclaré, avant d’ajouter : « Si Trump n’agit pas, le Congrès doit le faire ». À la Chambre des représentants, Hakeem Jeffries appelle lui aussi à agir rapidement et entend faire de l’intelligence artificielle une priorité pour son parti. Le débat ne se limite toutefois pas à une opposition entre républicains et démocrates. Au sein même du Parti démocrate, les approches divergent sur la manière de répondre aux risques associés aux technologies les plus avancées. Le sénateur Bernie Sanders défend notamment une position particulièrement stricte, souhaitant interdire la « superintelligence artificielle » et suspendre temporairement le développement de certains systèmes avancés. D’autres élus privilégient au contraire une réglementation ciblée, centrée sur les risques les plus immédiats. Plusieurs textes ont déjà été déposés à la Chambre avec le soutien d’élus des deux partis. Leur adoption reste toutefois incertaine, notamment en raison de la complexité institutionnelle du dossier. L’encadrement de l’intelligence artificielle touche en effet à de nombreux domaines : sécurité nationale, emploi, énergie, protection des consommateurs ou encore compétitivité économique. Ces questions relèvent de plusieurs commissions parlementaires, ce qui complique la mise en place d’une approche commune. Dans ce contexte, la réunion attendue au Conseil de sécurité de l’ONU pourrait constituer une nouvelle étape dans l’internationalisation du débat sur l’IA. Alors que les capacités des systèmes progressent rapidement, les États sont désormais confrontés à un double défi : favoriser l’innovation tout en anticipant les risques susceptibles d’affecter la sécurité et les sociétés à l’échelle mondiale. The post ONU : l’IA au cœur des débats face aux risques pour l’humanité appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .
